jobs.title: Project Manager,  AI Model Enablement and Agentic SDLC (Remote)
jobs.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About The Role:

CrowdStrike is a fast-growing cybersecurity company that protects customers from breaches. We are investing in project managers who are energetic, curious, and flexible, and who can run large, complex, cross-functional programs in a fast-paced environment. As a TechOps AI Project Manager, you will drive the initiatives that bring AI models and agentic development practices into how our technology organization builds, ships, and operates software. You will work across Engineering, Security, Data Science, Legal, and IT to make dependencies visible, surface critical issues early, and drive them to resolution.

What You'll Do:

Project Leadership: Lead end-to-end execution of TechOps AI initiatives. These include onboarding and enabling AI models, coding assistants, and agent platforms, and rolling out agentic workflows across the SDLC (design, coding, code review, testing, release, and operations). Identify, track, and escalate critical issues until they are resolved.
AI Enablement Program Management: Plan and coordinate model access, evaluation, and approval processes. This covers vendor and model onboarding, security and privacy reviews, usage policies, cost and capacity management, and tooling integration. Track adoption and outcome metrics such as usage, developer productivity, quality, and cost.
Communication and Coordination: Align cross-functional teams and act as the bridge between technical and non-technical stakeholders. Translate fast-moving AI developments into clear plans, risks, and decisions. Own status reporting and communication for small to mid-size projects, and break down silos between engineering, security, and platform teams.
Change Management and Adoption: Drive adoption of new AI-assisted and agentic ways of working. This means building champion networks, training and communication plans, feedback loops, and playbooks that help engineers adopt these tools with confidence and appropriate guardrails.
Process Improvement: Thrive in an evolving, growing team and iterate often. Look for ways to improve program management processes, including applying AI and agents to PMO work such as planning, reporting, risk tracking, and dependency management.
Stakeholder Engagement: Build strong relationships with internal teams and external partners, including AI model providers and tooling vendors. Provide regular, honest updates on progress, risks, and outcomes.

What You'll Need:

US Citizen or Green Card holder
4+ years of program or project management experience, ideally in software engineering, technical operations, developer productivity, or platform organizations.
Experience owning a program or portfolio of products or features: scoping requirements, planning milestones, and serving as an active resource for technical teams.
Working knowledge of the modern SDLC (CI/CD, code review, testing, release management) and of how AI coding assistants, LLMs, and agents are changing it.
Familiarity with core AI concepts: model selection and evaluation, prompt and context management, agent frameworks and tool use, and the cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs involved.
Demonstrable experience with organizational change management and adoption, ideally rolling out new tools or ways of working to large engineering populations.
Comfort navigating AI risk and governance topics, such as data handling, IP and licensing, model security, and responsible use, in partnership with Security, Legal, and Privacy teams.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders from individual engineers to senior leadership.
A seasoned team player who works through persistent obstacles instead of avoiding them.
Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-changing environment and to make logical, timely decisions with meticulous attention to detail.
Enjoys consensus-driven environments built on collaboration and open, honest communication, and works effectively with global, cross-divisional teams.
Self-directed learner who takes initiative as the AI landscape shifts.

Bonus Points

PMI, Agile Alliance, or equivalent certification.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools or building with LLMs and agents, or experience running AI/ML platform or developer-experience programs.
Experience with M&A and SaaS.
Experience at a high-tech, start-up, rapid-growth, or publicly traded company.
A genuine commitment to our mission. CrowdStrike doesn't have a mission statement. We are on a mission to protect our customers from breaches, and we want you to be eager to learn the details of our business.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
he Principal Technical Program Manager is accountable for the planning and execution of high-complexity technology programs and directly supporting the CTO. The Principal Technical Program Manager will work closely with Digital Product Managers and other stakeholders to coordinate delivery across cross-functional teams, ensuring that all relevant parties are involved, consulted, or informed. The Principal Technical Program Manager assists with vendor management and coordination. The Principal Technical Program Manager ensures that all non-functional requirements (such as reliability, scalability, security, etc) are documented, incorporated into plans, tracked, and executed appropriately. The Principal Technical Program Manager identifies and assists with assessing program needs and collaboratively identifies improvement opportunities. The Principal Technical Program Manager may work with multiple delivery teams in support of critical business functions.

Responsibilities

✔ Stakeholder Collaboration: Partners with stakeholders at all levels of the enterprise, and across divisions. Is perceived as a credible, strong leader, able to drive change, influence, and educate at all levels of the enterprise to achieve strategy-aligned outcomes. Partners with Procurement to negotiate vendor contracts; reviews areas of risk, interfaces with Vendor management.

40%

✔ Solution Management: In the context of complex enterprise programs and projects, works to ensure end-to-end solutions are implemented in alignment with enterprise strategy and architectural standards and practices. Develops comprehensive solution plans and articulates their dependencies, tradeoffs, risks, and merits to all stakeholders. Partners with Product Managers to ensure program or project plans are aligned with product roadmaps.

20%

✔ Project Management: Possesses strong Project Management skills and experience. Holds others accountable to drive programs/projects to successful execution of agreed-upon outcomes. Ensures that scope and schedule, including changes, are well understood by all interested parties. Coordinates requirements and deliverables across multiple teams, helping to resolve conflicts, dependencies, and technical tradeoffs and ensure teams understand broad, architecture and enterprise-level priorities and how that affects sequencing. Drives change and manages change with limited friction.

15%

✔ Communication: Communicates frequently and capably with a diverse audience, tailoring channel and message depending on needs and desired outcomes. Is influential and can drive change with minimal direct authority. Expertly articulates complex technical needs in a way that is understood by a non-technical audience. Drives understanding of and communicates the end user impact of technology projects.

15%

✔ Professional Development: Utilizes learning events and online learning opportunities to develop and enhance core competencies related to the role. Mentors others.

10%

Typical Years of Experience

10-15 years of cumulative, relevant experience

Specialty Education Required

College degree or equivalent work experience.

jobs.title: Program Manager
jobs.description:
Akima Data Management is seeking a highly qualified Program Manager to lead a multidisciplinary team supporting mission-critical cybersecurity, information technology, and operational services. This position requires a hands-on leader who will be onsite full-time, providing direct supervision, guidance, and operational oversight to ensure all contract requirements are met with the highest standards of quality, performance, and customer satisfaction.

Responsibilities

Lead contract execution, workforce planning, staffing, quality assurance, budget tracking, operational reporting, and stakeholder engagement to ensure successful program delivery.
Direct the development and maintenance of cybersecurity strategies, plans, standard operating procedures (SOPs), performance metrics and executive dashboards.
Manage Risk Management Framework (RMF) activities, Assessment and Authorization (A&A/CATO) processes, FISMA compliance, NIST control implementation, audit support, and POA&M remediation efforts.
Oversee enterprise risk management activities, including risk register maintenance, cybersecurity assessments, scorecards, incident reporting, and risk mitigation planning.
Coordinate and evaluate penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, and red, blue, and purple team exercises to strengthen security posture.
Provide leadership for Zero Trust initiatives, IPv6 transition efforts, enterprise security architecture, and cybersecurity engineering teams.
Guide cloud security strategy and architecture across Azure and Microsoft 365 environments, ensuring compliance with federal cybersecurity requirements and best practices.
Manage vulnerability scanning, remediation programs, IAVM compliance activities, and cybersecurity compliance reporting.
Oversee the implementation and operation of security technologies, including firewalls, secure web gateways (SWG), endpoint protection platforms, antivirus solutions, and Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems.
Direct Security Operations Center (SOC) activities, including incident response, digital forensics, threat monitoring, investigation, and executive reporting.
Manage Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) programs, including authentication, authorization, privileged access, and Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) services.
Lead disaster recovery (DR) and continuity of operations (COOP) planning, testing, exercises, and recovery operations to ensure mission resilience.
Establish and monitor service level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), operational metrics, and performance reporting to support continuous service improvement.
Serve as the primary interface with government stakeholders, executives, technical teams, and external partners to communicate program status, risks, issues, and strategic objectives.
Ensure all cybersecurity operations, engineering, and governance activities align with contractual requirements, agency policies, and federal regulatory standards.
Contribute to Request for Information, Request for Proposal and other administrative requests from executive staff.

Qualifications

An Active Top Secret clearance with the ability to obtain an SCI eligibility.
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, System Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Technology, or Management Information Systems
7+ years of experience managing cybersecurity engineering, vulnerability management, and compliance reporting programs.
5+ years of experience leading RMF, A&A/CATO, FISMA, NIST, and audit-compliance activities.
5+ years of experience overseeing SOC operations, incident response, and enterprise security monitoring.
5+ years of experience implementing Zero Trust architectures and cloud security solutions in Azure and Microsoft 365 environments.
Strong expertise in risk management, stakeholder engagement, performance metrics, and executive-level reporting.
IAM level III certification such as CISSP, CISM, or equivalent.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

2026-27262

Benefits

Regular - The company offers a comprehensive benefits program, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, 401(k) and a range of other voluntary benefits. Paid Time Off (PTO) is offered to regular full-time and part-time employees.

Work Where it Matters

Akima Data Management (ADM), an Akima company, is not just another federal IT contractor. As an Alaska Native Corporation (ANC), our mission and purpose extend beyond our exciting federal projects as we support our shareholder communities in Alaska.

At ADM, the work you do every day makes a difference in the lives of our 15,000 Iñupiat shareholders, a group of Alaska natives from one of the most remote and harshest environments in the United States.

For our shareholders,
ADM provides support and employment opportunities and contributes to the survival of a culture that has thrived above the Arctic Circle for more than 10,000 years.

For our government customers,
ADM delivers agile and innovative cloud and IT services and solutions that enable mission dominance.

As an ADM employee,
you will be surrounded by a challenging, yet supportive work environment that is committed to innovation and diversity, two of our most important values. You will also have access to our comprehensive benefits and competitive pay in addition to growth opportunities and excellent retirement options.

jobs.title: Mobilization Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

We’re on a journey to advance how health happens with technologies that support clinicians, inspire innovation, empower patients, and save lives. Our mission? To create a human-centric healthcare experience powered by unified global data. It’s a big challenge, but big challenges are what we do best. We’re already transforming some of the world’s largest health systems—helping them turn data into lifesaving decisions and better patient care. We want people just as dedicated as we are making history with the advancement of Federal Healthcare systems. If you’re excited about making healthcare more human, you’ve come to the right place. 

Oracle Health Government Services is seeking a Mobilization Project Manager to join our mission-driven organization. In this role, you will be responsible for leading project startup readiness across its federal portfolio. This role engages early in the pursuit lifecycle and partners with Federal Sales, Delivery Operations, and account program leaders to translate pursuit commitments into actionable, delivery-ready mobilization plans.

You will establish the operational foundation for new projects, coordinating project setup, initial financial requirements, stakeholder alignment, documentation, risk management, and kickoff planning. Working across a matrixed organization, you will clarify ownership, resolve readiness gaps, and coordinate a structured transition from pursuit to delivery.

By developing a consistent, scalable mobilization approach, you will help reduce startup delays, strengthen accountability, protect early project performance, and enable delivery teams to begin execution promptly upon award.

Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

Engage with Federal Sales, Delivery Operations, and program leaders during the pursuit lifecycle to identify mobilization needs, milestones, resource requirements, and dependencies. Identify participating lines of business and obtain confirmation of accountable owners, resource commitments, deliverables, and cross-business dependencies.
Assess mobilization requirements for new awards and contract modifications, tailoring the approach to the scope, complexity, and delivery impact of the change.
Develop and maintain a standardized mobilization checklist that supports consistent startup practices while accommodating program-specific requirements.
Coordinate project code creation and initial financial setup with Finance and other stakeholders, securing required approvals at the appropriate stage.
Coordinate staffing, onboarding, access, procurement, subcontractor, and financial readiness activities with responsible functional teams, as applicable.
Establish stakeholder and point-of-contact maps, including roles, responsibilities, escalation paths, and decision-making authority.
Create and organize project documentation and SharePoint structures to support collaboration, visibility, and an effective handoff to delivery teams.
Identify, document, and track key risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and decisions; escalate gaps that could affect launch readiness or early performance.
Develop the initial kickoff and transition plan, including meeting cadence, communications, required documentation, and handoff expectations.
Facilitate readiness reviews and cross-functional working sessions to resolve outstanding actions and confirm preparedness for project launch.
Coordinate the transition to delivery leadership, confirming ownership and acceptance of startup documentation, open actions, and ongoing responsibilities.
Track mobilization progress, communicate status to leadership, and incorporate lessons learned into reusable templates, tools, and processes.
Close mobilization after agreed exit criteria are met and remaining actions and responsibilities have been formally transferred.

Top skills or competencies to be successful:

Executive presence and communication skills
Attention to detail with strong organizational skills
Project mobilization and planning: Ability to translate evolving pursuit information into practical startup plans, milestones, and readiness criteria.
Cross-functional leadership and influence: Ability to align teams and drive accountability within a matrixed organization.
Operational and financial coordination: Understanding of project setup, financial dependencies, and the controls needed to support timely execution.
Risk management and problem-solving: Ability to anticipate startup barriers, evaluate dependencies, and resolve or escalate issues promptly.
Communication and stakeholder management: Clear, concise communication with sales, program leaders, delivery teams, and executive stakeholders.
Process improvement and organization: Ability to create repeatable practices, maintain accurate documentation, and manage competing priorities.

Education, certifications, or experience (preferred/required):

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Law, Public Administration, Accounting, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).
10+ years of experience relevant to the position, including at least 3 years of project management experience.
Demonstrated ability to apply sound project management principles and coordinate complex initiatives involving multiple stakeholders.
Experience coordinating project startup, implementation readiness, operational transitions, or comparable cross-functional activities.
Demonstrated success working in a matrixed environment and influencing stakeholders without direct reporting authority.
Experience developing project plans, tracking risks and dependencies, maintaining project documentation, and communicating progress to leadership.
Strong organizational, analytical, negotiation, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively through ambiguity.
US Citizenship is required with an ability to obtain and maintain a government security clearance.

jobs.title: Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
jobs.description:
The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
will partner with senior leaders across Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) to translate research insights into strategic recommendations for OPG and OFR staff, faculty and academic leadership, and other DAR colleagues, informing the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of prospective UHNW individual and foundation donors to Johns Hopkins University and Medicine.

Reporting to the Office of Principal Gifts (OPG) with a dotted line to Prospect Research within the Office of Advancement Services (OAS), this position will be matrixed to support the Office of Foundation Relations (OFR), with a focus on prospective ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals, foundations, family offices, financial institutions, and other key philanthropic partners. This individual will possess deep subject matter expertise in foundation research, wealth screenings, relationship mapping, and due diligence best practices.

The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst is responsible for partnering with the Office of Principal Gifts to implement and lead a comprehensive program of prospect identification, prospect analysis, and prospect monitoring. The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will conduct and advise others that are conducting research and ensure that the research meets the highest standards of confidentiality, quality, accuracy, and timeliness along with utmost attention to detail.

The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will apply, and model for others, excellent research, writing, presentation and organizational skills and implements new ways to secure and analyze information and leverage existing relationships to make connections to high-net-worth potential prospects. The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will work independently as well as collaboratively as a senior/lead member of the team.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Portfolio and Pipeline Management

Support portfolio reviews through partnerships with Development Research. This includes providing key information about managed prospects to support portfolio management and strategy discussions, in addition to capturing relevant data in the CRM.

Relationship Management Reporting

Generate reports that provide accurate projections of gifts in the pipeline and snapshots of the prospect pool and strategies. This will require the ability to query and compile CRM data for portfolio and pipeline projects as well as monthly, quarterly, and annual office reports.

Orient and Train Colleagues

Serve as the key trainer and technical support for DAR staff, supporting fundraisers across all business units. This includes disseminating and communicating changes in business practices (as needed) to administrative staff, documenting standard operating procedures, coordinating training schedules, and managing user roles in the CRM for incoming and outgoing DAR staff.

Build Internal Relationships

Develop and maintain effective work relationships with various colleagues and work as an effective RMPA team member. This includes responding to routine requests for information, providing answers to problems and/or inquiries relating to donors and prospects, and collaborating with gift officers to solicit input and explain database decisions.
Identify and cultivate key relationships within the Office of Advancement Services that enable the efficient execution of essential tasks to support data integrity and reporting.

Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties listed above, the Sr. Prospect and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
will:

Proactively identify new UHNW individual and foundation prospects with transformational giving capacity, using existing database resources and fee-based tools. We are a growth stage company that creates software solutions combining lean principles, predictive and prescriptive analytics, and machine learning to transform hospital and infusion center operations. More than 190 health systems and over 1,200 hospitals and centers across 49 states rely on our award-winning products and expert change management services to increase patient access, decrease wait times, and reduce healthcare delivery costs. We have raised more than $300 million from top-tier investors such as Bain Capital, Insight Partners, and Goldman Sachs. We have been named among the top 100 AI companies in the world.

Please note that while this role is listed as available for remote, we are currently employing in the following states:
AK, AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, FL, GA, IA, IL, IN, KS, KY, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MO, MT, NC, NH, NJ, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, WV
.
If your state is not listed, we may not be able to proceed with your application. We have offices in Santa Clara, CA and Charlotte, NC for employees who prefer to work regularly or occasionally from an office.

Join our Customer Onboarding team, where we partner with hospitals and health systems to implement technology that improves patient flow, optimizes capacity, and helps patients get the right care at the right time.

As a Senior Program Manager supporting Inpatient Flow, you will own healthcare technology implementations from pre-kickoff through go-live, serving as the primary driver of the project plan and day-to-day execution. You will bring together customer and LeanTaaS teams to manage the many interconnected pieces of a successful implementation—from discovery and technical readiness to workflow alignment, testing, training, go-live preparation, and launch.

You will build and manage detailed project plans, drive customer meetings and decisions, coordinate clinical and technical workstreams, manage risks and dependencies, and ensure teams remain aligned and accountable to their commitments. You’ll anticipate what could impact the implementation, create clear paths to resolution, and keep customers and internal stakeholders informed and moving forward.

Our implementations range from individual hospitals to complex, enterprise-wide deployments spanning multiple workflows, facilities, and stakeholder groups. You will partner closely with Clinical Workflow Implementation Managers, Product Implementation, Data Engineering, Customer Success and customer teams to bring structure and accountability to each engagement and ensure customers are prepared for a successful go-live.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Lead Customer Implementations

Own and lead a portfolio of complex Inpatient Flow implementations from kickoff through go-live and transition to Customer Success

Build, maintain, and execute detailed implementation plans, including milestones, deliverables, dependencies, resources, decisions, and timelines

Lead implementations that span multiple workflows in multiple hospitals across a health system

Run customer and internal implementation meetings, establish clear action items and owners, and drive accountability for commitments across customer and LeanTaaS teams

Coordinate discovery, technical implementation, workflow design, training, testing, readiness, and go-live activities across all implementation workstreams

Maintain implementation momentum by proactively following up on deliverables, resolving blockers, and ensuring decisions are made when needed

Drive high-quality implementations by ensuring consistent execution against established standards, proactively identifying gaps, and maintaining a high bar for customer experience and delivery excellence

Coordinate and participate in onsite meetings and activities

Manage Risk, Dependencies & Escalations

Continuously assess implementation health and proactively identify risks, dependencies, resource constraints, and decisions that could impact delivery

Develop and drive mitigation plans before risks become implementation delays or customer escalations

Identify and escalate issues requiring additional leadership, product, technical, or clinical support and ensure they remain actively managed through resolution

Manage changes to implementation scope and timelines, clearly communicating impacts and establishing alignment on the path forward

Maintain clear documentation of decisions, risks, action items, dependencies, and customer commitments throughout the implementation

Provide internal and customer stakeholders with clear, consistent visibility into implementation status, risks, accomplishments, and next steps

Drive Customer & Cross-Functional Alignment

Build strong working relationships with customer project leaders, executives, clinical leaders, operational stakeholders, and technical teams

Facilitate customer governance and implementation meetings that drive decisions, resolve open issues, and maintain alignment across stakeholders

Partner closely with Clinical Workflow Implementation Managers to incorporate workflow transformation, change management, training, and adoption activities into the overall implementation plan

Coordinate across Product Implementation, Data Engineering, Product, Customer Success, and other LeanTaaS teams to ensure workstreams and dependencies remain aligned

Navigate competing priorities and differing stakeholder perspectives while maintaining focus on implementation goals and customer outcomes

Ensure a thorough handoff to Customer Success at the completion of implementation, including outcomes, open items, commitments, risks, and opportunities for continued optimization

Understand the overall implementation strategy and translate it into a delivery approach that aligns project execution with customer needs, implementation goals, and desired business outcomes

Contribute to Implementation Excellence

Apply established implementation methodologies, tools, and best practices consistently across customer engagements

Identify opportunities to improve implementation processes, templates, tools, and documentation based on lessons learned from customer engagements

Share implementation insights and best practices with the broader team to improve consistency and execution across future implementations

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent years of related experience) in Business, Healthcare Administration, or a related field

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification

5+ years of hands-on project or program management experience leading complex healthcare implementations

Experience directly managing implementations through the full lifecycle, from kickoff and discovery through testing, training, go-live, and transition

Experience leading health system-wide initiatives involving multiple hospitals, workstreams, stakeholder groups, or technology solutions

Strong project management fundamentals, including project planning, dependency management, risk mitigation, issue management, scope management, and stakeholder communication

Demonstrated ability to manage multiple customer implementations and priorities simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail

Proven ability to drive accountability and results across cross-functional teams without direct authority

Experience working directly with executives, clinical leaders, operational teams, technical teams, and project stakeholders within hospitals or health systems

Ability to translate complex implementation details into clear project plans, decisions, risks, and next steps

Strong communication, facilitation, problem-solving, and organizational skills

Proficiency with project management tools and methodologies

Resourceful, results-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, customer-facing environment

Willingness to travel 30–40% of the time

BONUS POINTS IF YOU HAVE

Experience implementing enterprise healthcare technology or SaaS solutions

Experience with inpatient hospital operations, patient flow, capacity management, or related operational workflows

Experience managing multi-product or multi-site implementations across large health systems

Experience working in JIRA and Smartsheet

Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, or other process improvement training or certification

WHAT YOU'LL GET

Intellectual and emotional satisfaction of solving tough operational problems in healthcare while improving patient access and saving lives!

Competitive compensation package that includes base salary, target bonus, and stock options

401(k) Match

Comprehensive healthcare benefits

Generous Paid Time Off and Parental Leave

, CA global headquarters. Hybrid or remote work is open to the right candidate.

ustomer Leadership

Business Operations Manager

Operations

Director of Business Operations

About Plug

Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We've facilitated over $150M in EV sales and raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Why Plug

You'll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
You'll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
You'll be part of an AI-native company. We're rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.
You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
You'll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Business Operations Manager to be a force multiplier for our BizOps Director: someone who can take an ambiguous, cross-functional problem, build the trust to step into another team's operations, and drive a data-driven fix.

You'll own cross-functional projects end to end, scoping them, driving implementation, and measuring success. You'll partner directly with functional leaders (Sales, Dealer Success, Ops) to diagnose operational challenges and help fix them.

What You'll Own

Cross-Functional Project Ownership

Lead cross-functional initiatives from scoping through execution.
Drive accountability across teams you don't formally manage. Keep initiatives moving, surface risks early, and make sure deliverables ship.
Take on problems that arrive as symptoms ("this handoff keeps breaking," "onboarding is too slow") and figure out what's actually going on to propose a fix.

Operational Partnership

Partner directly with functional leaders to diagnose inefficiencies in how their teams operate.
Analyze data to size a problem and diagnose the root cause.
Design and implement fixes such as new agentic workflows, automations, and SOPs.
Lead and facilitate department operations, such as weekly business reviews.
Act on diagnosed daily metric alerts.

What You'll Bring

4-7 years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, consulting, or a high-growth startup operations role. Marketplace or automotive experience is a plus.
A track record of owning ambiguous problems end-to-end.
Strong stakeholder management: you can walk into a team you don't manage, build credibility fast, and drive change without formal authority.
Comfortable with data (SQL a plus) and analytics.
Excellent written and verbal communication. A structured thinker who can bring clarity to a messy situation.
Bias toward action, low ego, and thrives in zero-to-one ambiguity.

Research consistently shows that people from under-represented groups are more likely to talk themselves out of applying if they don't meet 100% of the listed requirements. You don't need to check every box. If this role excites you and you bring most of what's listed under "What You'll Bring," we want to hear from you.

Overview

Carollo Engineers is a leading engineering firm dedicated exclusively to water. For over 90 years, we've specialized in the planning, design, and construction of water, wastewater, stormwater, and reuse facilities, bringing innovative and sustainable solutions to the water sector's most complex challenges.

We work with water agencies, municipalities, utilities, research organizations, and private companies across various industries, including technology, manufacturing, and beyond. These clients choose Carollo because we employ some of the most knowledgeable and experienced professionals in the world. When you join our team, you'll work alongside industry leaders who are advancing the science of water, protecting public health, and building resilient communities.

Carollo's vision is to be the best water consulting firm and the best place for you to build your career. If you're passionate about making a difference in this critical field, we invite you to explore a career with Carollo.

Responsibilities

Expand Carollo’s presence in the local stormwater market via targeted business development strategies, including growing specific client relationships and participating in select professional society activities.
Collaborate with the Stormwater Leads across the company to develop/implement strategy for continued stormwater growth and innovation across the company.
Manage planning and detailed design projects, including management of contract document production (i.e., plan sets and specifications), hydraulic and hydrologic calculations, report writing, and other activities needed to support the planning, design, and construction services for stormwater management facilities. Project may include pipelines, open channels, pump stations, channel stabilization, storage and treatment facilities, multi-benefit facilities, and other conveyance measures.
Collaborate with other engineering disciplines, designers, and scientists, among others, who support specific assignments.

10+ years of experience relating to stormwater and water resources projects
Minimum 5 years of experience managing a team to deliver planning and design solutions for urban stormwater management challenges.
Minimum 5 years of experience with client service and business development efforts, including project positioning, proposal preparation, interviews, and technical presentations
Familiarity with standard stormwater analysis tools, including HEC-RAS (1D/2D), HEC-HMS, ICM, FLO-2D, XPSWMM, ArcGIS, and Civil 3D.
Experience with the selection and optimization of multi-benefit urban storm water projects
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Strong team building skills
Ability to apply critical thinking
Ability to present to groups and communicate effectively with clients and project team
Proficiency in MS Word, Outlook, Excel, and PowerPoint

Master’s degree in Civil, Environmental, or Agricultural Engineering or other appropriate engineering major
Experience with FEMA floodplain delineation and submittal of Letters of Map Revision and Conditional Letters of Map Revision

would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the

posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee’s pay within the salary

range will be based on several factors including, but limited to, relevant education, qualifications,

certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or

organizational needs.

Strong SQL skills (any variant)

jobs.title: Digital Project Manager
jobs.description:
Viget is an independent digital agency that has been designing and building digital products and platforms since 1999. Our culture is ideal for lifelong learners seeking a variety of meaningful work, supportive collaboration with positive teammates, and a healthy work/life balance. We work from four offices (hybrid) and remote locations throughout the U.S., and enjoy a proven cadence of virtual and in-person meetings and retreats to build camaraderie and stay connected. We work with tech companies (like Robinhood and SpectrumAi), non-profits (like World Wildlife Fund and NPF), and consumer brands (like Stern Pinball and ESPN).

At Viget, Digital Project Managers are much more than just project coordinators -- they’re project leaders and lead consultants. They work collaboratively with clients to understand organization goals, define solutions, answer hard questions, and ensure the overall quality of a project. They facilitate tasking, budget management, and day-to-day communication with clients and internal teams. They are both empathetic and results-driven, cultivating a culture of efficiency, innovation, trust, and progress on their projects.

As a DPM at Viget, you’ll lead a variety of projects, including large-scale content sites, product design, and software development efforts. You’ll define and prioritize requirements, collaborate with our brilliant designers and developers, support user research and testing, lead quality assurance, and celebrate thrilling launches. More than any other role at Viget, you’ll contribute to all areas of a successful project.

You'll need to communicate, collaborate, and lead effectively. Here are the things we're looking for:

You’re a polished and persuasive communicator (without BS-ing). You consistently listen, make connections, write, and speak better than most people.
You were born with or have carefully cultivated an awareness of and appreciation for details.
You get made fun of by your friends because you’re “too” organized (as if THAT’S possible).
You meet deadlines across multiple, simultaneous projects.
You build long-term relationships with clients based on thorough planning, timely and professional communication, and intelligent problem-solving.
You’re solution-oriented. You don’t just identify problems, you synthesize solutions.
You’re comfortable closely managing project budgets. You can work with internal teams to manage their time within constraints, transparently communicate budget health to clients, and lead prioritization discussions to help clients understand tradeoffs and collaboratively identify solutions that work with their timelines and budgets.
You have a "thick skin" when the going gets tough. If and when conflicting demands emerge, you communicate diplomatically to reach a resolution.
You demonstrate integrity through your words and actions.
You love processes and plans, but you’re flexible. You can create an effective project plan and timeline, but are comfortable enough with ambiguity to adapt the plan when things change.

You'll also need to be able to work well in our technical environment. Here are things we’re looking for (note: we recognize that you may not have done all of these before, and that's okay):

You have worked in a fast-paced software development environment before, whether at an agency or product company.
You know how the web works and how a web app works, which means you’re aware of technical constraints when talking to clients. You don’t hesitate to ask a lot of questions in order to define the functionality of what we’re building.
You can break down a set of wireframes into actionable tasks for back-end and front-end developers. You’re passionate about finding innovative, efficient, and effective ways to document those tasks.
You can shepherd often-vague client requests and ideas through the definition process. You know when to rely on a UX designer, but you’re comfortable thinking through logic and creating useful documentation of that logic.
You’re able to describe workflows and tasks purely from an end user’s perspective, helping developers make informed implementation decisions.
You’ve performed QA. You can distinguish a bug from a functional update from a new feature request.
Generally, successful candidates will have between 3 and 8 years of experience managing digital projects. If the role has piqued your interest and you think you’d be a fit, but don’t quite meet the requirements, we still encourage you to reach out.

Everyone At Viget

Embodies our core values of integrity, work ethic, collaboration, creativity, and lifelong learning.
Values mentorship, learning, and sharing knowledge.
Writes and speaks clearly and effectively when collaborating with teammates and clients.
Believes in and supports our commitment to building a diverse and inclusive company.

Compensation And Benefits

Annual base salary of $70,000 - $100,000 (mid level) or $90,000 - $120,000 (senior) per year depending on location, skills, and experience
Additional comp available via spot performance bonuses, sales referrals, and new hire referrals
401(k) retirement plan matching up to 4%
100% company-paid health and dental coverage for you and your family
Stipends for wellness (apps, gyms, etc.) and connectivity (mobile phone or home internet)
15 days PTO (20 after 2 years), 9 paid holidays, and 2 community service days per year
Up to $2,000/year in conference and training (professional development) budget

How To Apply

Apply by completing the application form. We expect you may use AI for research, prep, and proofreading during the job application process. We use AI daily and believe that building AI skills is essential, but at this stage we need to get to know you
. To that end, unless directed otherwise, we expect you will not submit AI-generated answers or assignments (writing, coding, designing) nor use AI for real-time help during interviews. Using AI tools to misrepresent your knowledge, ability, or experience is unethical. It’s also impractical and short-sighted since once you’re in the role you’ll often need to think and communicate in real-time without AI help. As a small team with high standards for quality and, above all, integrity, we ask that you write your own application answers, submit work that reflects the real you, and share openly how you used AI in the application process if at all.

We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications and are actively seeking people from underrepresented groups to join our team.

readiness.

Lead cross-functional execution of in-house and vendor hardware development,

Improve program operating cadence and execution practices across multiple concurrent

Experience coordinating engineering, validation, manufacturing, and other partners

electrical, software, and systems architectures.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Transfer Program Manager
jobs.description:
Introduction to the job

Over the past decades, ASML has grown exponentially, and as we rely heavily on our supply chain, so has our supply chain ecosystem. In the coming years we expect further growth that will require a transformation of large parts of our Supply Chain. In order to tackle this strategic challenge and help Shape & Drive the transformation in our supply chain we created the ‘Supply Chain Transformation’ department within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement. From this department, a team of professionals in Supply Chain management disciplines will drive engagements / change programs in our supply chain and be supported with specific competencies from across ASML.

As a Supply Chain Transfer Manager, you will lead cross-functional teams responsible for managing critical supply chain transfers. Your goal is to ensure the timely and reliable availability of materials, working closely with stakeholders across technical and operational disciplines. You’ll drive project progress, safeguard supply continuity, and play a key role in managing transitions in our supply chain.

Role and responsibilities

The Supply Transfer Manger is responsible for:

Lead and manage {{b}}complex, multidisciplinary technical supply chain transfer projects{{/b}} from initial planning through execution, stabilization, and closure.
Develop and maintain {{b}}integrated project plans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, critical paths, and risk mitigation actions{{/b}} to ensure transfers remain on schedule.
Lead cross-sector alignment on {{b}}technical test, qualification, and release requirements{{/b}} throughout the transfer, ensuring dependencies, risks, and readiness criteria are understood and managed across engineering, quality, supply chain, and supplier teams.
Identify gaps in technical documentation, requirements, and transfer readiness; own the documentation process and drive cross-functional teams to resolve gaps, clarify requirements, and achieve timely closure.
Manage the complexity of evolving technology and changing technical requirements that may impact product transfer scope, timing, and execution, proactively assessing dependencies and adjusting transfer plans to maintain continuity and project objectives.
Manage and lead multidisciplinary technical orientated cross-sector transfer team
Establish clear project governance and align with internal and external stakeholders on goals and plans
Collaborating to create and maintain the transfer portfolio
Supporting resource planning to ensure successful transfer execution
Set up a full phasing out/transfer product overview including (non) transfer, including
Capacity alignment across n-tier supply chain
Logistic risk mitigation such as buffer strategy and last buy decisions
Definition of technical release procedure per product category with transfer team and execute these
Solid input on phasing out negotiations to the Sourcing team
Proactively execute supply chain risk analysis and execute action plans to mitigate risk; ensuring Material availability at all phases of the program and right quality before and after shipment / ensuring on time delivery during the project
Manage escalations within transfers to solve bottlenecks in supply chain and avoid re-occurrence

Education and experience

Degree in engineering or related technical field. Master’s highly preferred.
10+ years relevant professional experience in a high-tech NPI environment.
Strong background in industrialization, supply chain, or sourcing.
Proven expertise in project management and familiarity with re-allocating products or production
Experience collaborating in cross-functional, technical environments to drive supply chain improvements
Experience directly managing suppliers and building trusting relationships
Risk management experience and business continuity

Skills

Familiarity with key technical concepts and technical understanding to engage effectively with engineering teams
Stakeholder Alignment & Decision Making
Project Governance
Portfolio Management
Strategic Sourcing Collaboration
Transfer Negotiation Support
Business Continuity Planning
Risk Mitigation Strategy Development
Excellent stakeholder management and relationship building skills
Conceptual thinker on strategic level
Strong analytical skills
Convincing / negotiation skills
Pragmatic and result driven
Pro-active attitude, drive for improvement

Other information

To be effective as Supply Transfer Manager requires close cooperation with involved suppliers and hence occasional travel for business is required.

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement engages with our supply chain partners to drive their (operational) performance on metrics on the QLTCS domains (Quality, Logistics, Technology, Cost, and Sustainability). The activities of ‘running the business’ are part of the ‘supplier clusters’. Across the cluster teams and regions, the Supply Chain Transformation team runs the ‘changing the business’ activities.

$162,750-238,700

jobs.description:
Company Description

Stone Research Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit research institute founded in 1991 by Kevin R. Stone, MD, and dedicated to developing innovative orthopaedic treatments that help people stay active. The organization focuses on research, development, and education to create regenerative therapies that accelerate healing and address arthritis. Its vision is to transform scientific discovery into treatments that prevent, manage, and ultimately cure joint disease. Team members collaborate with clinicians, scientists, and partners to advance impactful, patient-centered solutions in musculoskeletal health. Learn more at www.stoneresearch.org.

Role Description

The Stone Research Foundation pioneers regenerative orthopaedic treatments to treat, prevent, and cure arthritis. We are seeking a Research Program Manager to drive collaborative research activities, translate scientific innovation into meaningful progress, and connect research, regulatory, and funding efforts—advancing groundbreaking discoveries toward the next generation of orthopaedic care. This position will report to the Sr. Director of Research and Operations. This role is full-time onsite.

Key Responsibilities

Research Operations
· Oversee major study operations activities
· Review and manage study budgeting
· Prepare study protocols and design preclinical and clinical studies
· Track regulatory progress and ensure completion of IND-enabling activities
· Maintain all regulatory documents and records
· Perform statistical analyses as needed to report study data for scientific dissemination and publication
· Assist and work closely with the Sr. Director, Research and Operations to execute activities efficiently at a high level
· May require occasional travel to study sites and conferences with the Sr. Leadership

Project and Program Management
· Serve as an adept project manager for all internal and external partnerships
· Set meetings, deadlines, and overall smooth flow of projects
· Create long-term and short-term plans, including setting and tracking milestones and deliverables
· Serve as the point of contact for all SRF research partnerships
· Analyze and account for possible risks when developing project milestones

Funding and Grant Applications
· Coordinate cross-functional efforts across grant application and submission, including milestone-setting and timelines, setting budgets and activities across internal and external partners
· Take ownership of grant writing and submission

Scientific Communication
· Quickly and efficiently compose and edit presentations and manuscripts for publications
· Prepare abstracts, posters, and slides for conference presentations
· Contribute to presentations compiled for key stakeholders, fundraising, and development purposes
· Effectively and efficiently distill complex scientific concepts into digestible communications for non-scientific team members and external stakeholders

Patient Interface
· Obtain IRB consent and enroll patients in studies on occasion, as needed
· Answer patient questions regarding research on an as-needed basis

Qualifications

· Advanced degree (M.S., MPH, etc.) strongly preferred
· Advanced degree with 5+ years of experience or bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of direct experience desired
· Preference for previous orthopaedic research experience; however, any area of research experience will count toward years of experience
· Skilled in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel
· Comfortable conducting statistical analyses and using software including: GraphPad, ANOVA, t-test, and survival analyses
· Deep experience developing study budgets and tracking budget activities
· Regulatory: Comfort with IND and medical device requirements set by FDA and EMA
· Sound understanding of GCP, GMP, and GLP requirements and ICH standards
· Demonstrated experience in grant writing and management
· Proven manuscript and scientific writing experience
· Previous experience in preclinical and clinical experimental design and protocol design
· Project Management tools: preferred experience using Asana
· IRB submission and patient consent experience

Personal Characteristics

· Strong team player with demonstrated experience in leading and contributing to cross-functional teams
· Proactive and self-starting
· Willingness to wear multiple hats, be resourceful, and always think of ways to improve
· Adaptable and a quick thinker

Ride BART to a satisfying career that lets you both: 1) make a difference to Bay Area residents, and 2) enjoy excellent pay, benefits, and employment stability. BART is looking for people who like to be challenged, work in a fast-paced environment, and have a passion for connecting riders to work, school and other places they need to go. Pay Rate
:

Senior Manager of Engineering Programs

Days Off

Saturday and Sunday

Who May Apply

All current BART employees and Future BART employees.

Current Assignment

The San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District (BART) is seeking highly qualified candidates for the Project Manager Accessibility position. The ideal candidates will possess results-oriented engineering and construction experience to manage complex capital improvement projects within its Accessibility Improvement Program. This position will be responsible for accessibility planning, design review, code interpretation and regulatory compliance, and managing the AIP. They will provide District staff with guidance in accessibility and inclusive design principles including communicating and coordinating with internal and external stakeholders to achieve optimal accommodation for all users.

Key responsibilities include defining project scope and budget; managing design teams and resolving stakeholder concerns; supporting procurement activities; and overseeing construction management teams through project closeout to successfully deliver the AIP program.

The position serves as the District’s lead accessibility resource, reviewing and advising on projects, policies, and procedures to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and industry best practices. The candidates will provide input and assistance in resolving accessibility-related issues across the District’s planning, design, construction, maintenance, and operating entities.

The Most Qualified Candidates For This Position Will Have Highly Developed Competencies In The Following Areas, Which Will Be Reinforced In The Related Work Experience And Will Be Articulated During The Selection Process

Licensed Professional Engineer – Registration as a Professional Civil Engineer in the State of California.
Engineering and Design Expertise – Demonstrated experience managing engineering and/or architectural projects through planning, design, and implementation phases.
Transportation Project Management – Proven experience managing complex projects in an operating transportation, transit, or public infrastructure environment.
Accessibility and Inclusive Design – Extensive knowledge of accessibility regulations and inclusive design best practices.
Communication and Stakeholder Engagement – Excellent written and verbal communication skills and strong public speaking ability.

Selection and Application Process

All applicants must apply online at www.bart.gov/jobs
. Applications must be completed in full and include all requested information, including dates of employment, positions held, hours worked, and a detailed description of duties performed.

Applicants may attach a resume to provide supplemental information; however, the resume does not substitute for completing the application form in its entirety. Only information included in the application at the time of submission will be used to determine whether applicants meet the minimum qualifications for the position. All application materials must be submitted by the closing date and time listed on the job announcement. Applications received after the closing deadline will not be considered.

Applicants who require assistance with the online application process may contact the Talent Acquisition Division
at (510) 464-6112 or employment@bart.gov .

The selection process for this position may include one or more of the following: a skills or performance demonstration, written examination, and/or panel or individual interview.

All applications will be reviewed by the Talent Acquisition Division to determine whether applicants meet the established Minimum Qualifications (MQs). Applicants who meet the MQs may be referred to the hiring department for further evaluation as part of the selection process.

The selected candidate must demonstrate a work history reflecting reliability and dependability and may be required to provide copies of certificates, diplomas, or other documentation required by law, including proof of authorization to work in the United States.

Pre-employment processing will include a background check. This requirement does not apply to current full-time District employees unless the position requires additional evaluations or clearances.

Examples of Duties

Manages BART’s Accessibility Improvement Program’s engineering design and construction projects or programs in assigned areas from conceptual design through completion; project areas may include rail car procurement and rehabilitation, stations construction and rehabilitation, automated fare collection, and transit systems and structures design and construction.
Develops and directs project work standards from design through final program and equipment acceptance.
Develops and directs the implementation of goals, objectives, policies and procedures in assigned project areas.
Plans, organizes, assigns, reviews and evaluates the work of assigned District and contract staff; manages and directs the work of contract consultants.
Directs or participates in the preparation and review of designs, plans, specifications and cost estimates; ensures specifications and contract requirements comply with District standards and policies.
Identifies equipment or systems needs on assigned projects; evaluates functional requirements; reviews vendor and manufacturer design and specifications on project equipment and materials; coordinates equipment procurement and testing activities; oversees equipment installation.
As assigned, oversees contractor and consultant contracts; develops scope of work; prepares request for proposal; reviews proposals and makes recommendation on selection; assists in contract negotiation and preparation; monitors work activities to ensure compliance with contractual obligations.

Performs construction project management duties; prepares cost estimates; prepares and monitors project schedules and budgets; conducts field inspections as required; monitors work in progress; writes, approves, negotiates and executes contract changes; authorizes contract payments upon project completion.
Serves as the project liaison with other divisions, departments and outside agencies; negotiates and resolves project issues.
Provides responsible staff assistance for higher level management staff on projects and related matters.
Attends and participates in professional group meetings; stays abreast of new trends and innovations in the field of engineering design and construction.

Possession of a bachelor's degree in engineering or related field from an accredited college or university.

Professional Engineering (PE) license is required.

Additional professional experience as outlined above may be substituted for the education on a year-for- year basis. A college degree is preferred.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members.

Project Description

The Heart of Conservation Initiative
( HCI
) is a 5-year
global project
designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas.  

Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. 

This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation; and (v) monitoring and evaluation.

Job Description

LOCATION: This position will be based in Brazil, Kenya, or Cambodia.

Major Function

The Project Manager will lead the GCU’s support for the HCI partners and ensure successful delivery of all components. They will supervise staff in a Global Coordination Unit (GCU), provide day-to-day management of the project and, with support from the Partner Liaison, coordinate with ten (10)  Component 1 Partners, and partners and specialists in Components 2 through 5.  This is a unique role managing and representing a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous Peoples and local community partners’ priorities as well as meet GEF requirements. 

The Project Manager will report to the Senior Director, Conservation Areas, and Senior Director, Inclusive Conservation (Project Co-Leads)

Key Responsibilities

 Technical Delivery of Project Components:  
Component 1: Work with Component 1 partners to review and approve their annual work plans and budgets, provide technical inputs to their on-the-ground work, as needed, and support their self-strengthening plans.    
Component 2: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 2 with GCU staff support; Work with Component 1 partners to identify common capacity-strengthening needs and develop and implement a collective strengthening program.  
Component 3: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 3 with GCU staff support; Design and implement the Youth Policy Leaders program and work with Component 1 and 2 partners to identify policy processes and to enable effective, HCI-supported engagement therein.  
Support GCU staff to ensure successful delivery of Components 4 and 5.
 Project Management: 
Day-to-day management, monitoring, and evaluation of project activities and results as outlined in the CERDoc, Grant Agreement, and Annual Work Plan and Budget to achieve the project objective and targets in the Results Framework. 

Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:  

Ensure that the GCU holds regular virtual meetings with Component 1 (C1) partners and as required with additional partners involved in the other components,  
Manage the workflow for the Indigenous Global Steering Committee (IGSC), in collaboration with the Project Co-Leads. 
In collaboration with all project sub-grantees and partners, develop the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) for the global HCI for each project year, for no-objection from the WWF GEF Agency and approval by the IGSC.  
Share C1 Partners’ annual workplans and budgets for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency and for IGSC information.  Provide high-level oversight and monitoring of procurement and expenditure in line with the AWPB in collaboration with the Finance and Operations (FO) Manager.
Review progress of work plan and monitoring plan in collaboration with the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer.  
Responsible for organization of inception workshop and other critical project workshops and meetings. 
Manage the design and maintenance of a project website, and the development and implementation of a communications strategy in collaboration with the Communications and Knowledge Management (CKM) Officer. 
Provide support for project implementation support and learning visits and internal and external reviews/evaluations with relevant GCU staff.
Support the MEL Officer to organize annual reflection workshops to identify lessons learned and propose potential changes for adaptive management to ensure project results and indicator targets are reached. 
Troubleshoot with GCU staff, component partners and Project co-leads to address challenges and create enabling conditions for trusting partnerships and project success.
Maintain a project risk register, including identification of risks to project success and development of mitigation measures in coordination with C1 partners and other project partners.  
Prepare and execute a project exit plan, including hand-off of project equipment and resources, close of grants and agreements, consultations and communications with project partners and interested parties, and ensure sustainability of project results. 
Champion the promise and achievements of the project, elevating its contributions to systems change and Indigenous Peoples and local community-led partners whenever possible. 
Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment.
Staff management: 
Supervise the GCU staff including MEL Officer (crosscutting, especially components 1, 4 and 5), FO Manager (crosscutting), Environmental and Social Safeguards Officer (crosscutting, especially component 1), Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Officer (crosscutting , especially component 1), CKM Officer (crosscutting, especially components 2 and 4), Logistics and Administrative Assistant (crosscutting), and any other directly recruited staff or consultants.
Prepare TORs to recruit consultants, staff and sub-contracts in consultation with Project Co-Leads and for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency. 
Reporting: 
Collaborate with the MEL Officer to aggregate information from Component 1 Partner sub-projects and formulate semi-annual Project Progress Reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Prepare workshop reports following the inception and other critical project workshops.
Collaborate with the FO Manager to oversee the preparation and disbursement of sub-grants to Component 1 partners and grants and agreements under the other 4 components.  
Collaborate with the FO Manager to aggregate financial information from C1 Partners and oversee the development of quarterly financial reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Collaborate with the WWF network and partners to ensure co-finance reporting on a yearly basis. 
Prepare a Project Close Report.  
Quality Assurance: 
Provide quality assurance for project activities, including sub-grants. 
Provide quality assurance through review of reports and other products from partners, technical specialists, consultants, and staff.
Ensure implementation in line with the GEF and WWF standards and policies. 
Week-long, international travel may be expected on approximately a quarterly basis. 
Partnerships: 
Coordinate with co-financed projects and liaise with project partners to ensure co-financing commitments are realized.  
Attract additional partners and co-financing. 
Ensure smooth coordination and communication among all project partners, and with the Component 1 partners (the latter in collaboration with Partner Liaison). 
Manage stakeholder engagement and ensure gender and social inclusion considerations are fully integrated throughout project implementation in collaboration with the Social and Environmental Safeguards (ESS) and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Officers.  
Represent the project at conferences, meetings, and workshops. 

Qualifications

Key Competencies

Strategic Collaboration and Leadership. Able to lead and influence large and highly dispersed teams and coalitions, dealing with risk mitigation and conflict management.
Intercultural and adaptive management skills 
Results-oriented project management
Collaboration
Cross-cultural communication

Skills And Abilities

10 years of technical working experience, including at least five years of project management experience.  
Bachelor’s Degree; post-graduate degree in a relevant field preferred. 
At least five years’ experience supporting and working in solidarity with Indigenous people and local community organizations, and a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
Demonstrated ability to interact with Indigenous peoples and local community representatives, senior government, NGO, business, and donor staff. 
Experience with the Convention on Biological Diversity and/or other multilateral agreements and processes, focusing on biodiversity, Indigenous peoples’ and local communities’ rights, and finance. 
Experience delivering technical and financial reporting to donor agencies on large projects. 
Experience managing similar, complex, multi-stakeholder and multi-country projects.

Technical experience and knowledge in the thematic area of the project, such as Indigenous -led territorial stewardship, community-based sustainable development, etc.

Our leading SaaS-based Global Employment Platform™ enables clients to expand into over 180 countries quickly and efficiently, without the complexities of establishing local entities. Our diverse, remote-first teams are essential to our success. We empower our Dream Team members with flexibility and resources, fostering an environment where innovation thrives and every contribution is valued and celebrated.

The work you do here will positively impact lives around the world. We stand by our promise: Opportunity Made Possible. In addition to competitive compensation and benefits, we invite you to join us in expanding your skills and helping to reshape the future of work.

At G-P, we assist organizations in building exceptional global teams in days, not months—streamlining the hiring, onboarding, and management process to unlock growth potential for all.

About The Role

As our customer base evolves to serve large global enterprises, we are shifting from fragmented, regional ops handoffs to a dedicated, high-touch delivery model.

The Forward Deployed Operations Manager (FD-OM)
acts as the single operational point of contact for our enterprise clients and internal Customer Success teams. You will sit at the intersection of enterprise project management, global employment compliance, customer activation, and operational delivery—ensuring seamless global expansions and long-term customer satisfaction.

Internal Alignment: Coordinate within internal HR Ops regional teams in close partnership with Customer Success, Sales teams to align resources and streamline program execution

Global Compliance & Operational Delivery

Compliance Oversight: Navigate complex international labor laws, visa/immigration requirements, benefits administration, and localized employment contract - acting as a consultant to our Customers to deliver on value across multiple workstreams and tailor our offering to Customer’s needs

Risk Mitigation: Proactively identify and resolve operational blockers, regulatory risks, and payroll setup delays across multiple jurisdictions.

Adoption & Happiness: Drive client activation and platform adoption, ensuring a white-glove onboarding experience for both enterprise admins and international employees.
Escalations & Problem-Solving: Act as the direct escalation point for complex operational inquiries, resolving issues with high speed and precision.

Operational Scaling & Process Improvement

Playbook Development: Document and refine implementation playbooks, scalable workflows, and enterprise delivery standards to continuously decrease time-to-first-payroll.
Voice of Customer: Partner with Product and Engineering teams to feed enterprise client requirements back into the platform roadmap.

Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to thrive in ambiguous environments and translate complex regulatory/operational realities into simple, actionable steps for clients.

Preferred Requirements

International work experience across EMEA, LATAM, or APAC regions.

Core Competencies

Operational Agility: Unblocking localized compliance hurdles quickly without compromising governance.
Empathy & Drive: Delivering high customer satisfaction during high-stakes corporate expansions.

Success Metrics (KPIs)

Customer Satisfaction (CSAT / NPS): High satisfaction scores during the onboarding and implementation phase.
Implementation Accuracy: Zero compliance or payroll setup errors during the first pay run.
