jobs.title: Information Security Manager, Product & Platform Security
jobs.description:
Full-Time

In Person: Boston, MA Headquarters

Step into a pivotal Security Leadership
role at a fast-growing grid intelligence company.

LineVision’s customers include eight of the ten largest US utilities, which demand the highest levels of security in order to protect sensitive data and the electric grid from attack. You will lead LineVision to advance Product and Enterprise security to give customers confidence to rely on LineVision.

Reporting to the VP of Security, IT, and Quality, you will have broad autonomy over security engineering, security operations, controls execution, governance, and compliance. You and a Security Analyst will guide the security of our Products (AWS Platform, RS-1 optical and weather sensors) and Enterprise (SaaS platforms, IAM, endpoints, etc) across the full spectrum of security and compliance responsibilities, including annual SOC 2 Type II audits and ISO 27001 certifications, risk management, vulnerability management, incident response, penetration testing program, and customer security questionnaires. Partnering with IT, Platform, Hardware, and Customer Success, you will combine your vision and hands-on experience to build security into a strategic business advantage at LineVision.

If you want to build a security program that is seen as a strategic differentiator and wins customer trust, join us at LineVision, Built In Boston Best Places to Work
!

Please note: Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. This position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship.

What will you do?

Core Responsibilities And Key Performance Objectives

Compliance Program Ownership: Own the annual audit cycle for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 using the Vanta compliance platform, including all controls, internal audits, external audits, and nonconformity tracking to closure.
Risk Management & Governance: Lead the annual NIST CSF risk assessment, monthly Platform and Hardware risk reviews, and quarterly Governance, Risk & Compliance reviews. Maintain policies and report ISMS efficacy metrics to leadership.
Security Engineering: Conduct AWS cloud and Sensor penetration tests, ISA/IEC 62443 product security assessments, vendor and product risk assessments.
Security Operations: Oversee vulnerability management, CrowdStrike Falcon Complete detection rules, NextGen SIEM data feeds, and the MSSP relationship. Monitor open-source license compliance with FOSSA.
Incident Response & Resilience: Own the incident response program and plan, including the annual 3rd part tabletop, business continuity and disaster recovery exercises, and implementation of lessons learned.
Confidential Data Protection: Define and guide data management controls, ensuring rigorous application of policies and customer contractual obligations regarding confidential data. Partner with Platform, Hardware and IT to apply controls across all company systems and applications.
Customer & Sales Support: Lead responses to customer security questionnaires, contract security reviews, and customer-facing security presentations and material.
AI Security: Identify risks and define security standards for enterprise and product AI. Inform the AI governance program with risk assessments and recommendations.
Team Leadership: Coach and develop the security team.
Please note: This role may require participation in a compensated, rotational on-call schedule. Any on-call responsibilities would take effect after the onboarding period.

Current Projects

Within the first 3 months:

Establish operational rhythm with the security team, including 1-1s, goal-setting, and sprint planning.
Take ownership of the audit calendar, risk register, and security project portfolio.
Implement an intake and prioritization process for security work that surfaces trade-offs and schedule risk early.
Take over customer security questionnaires and contract reviews, and build a reusable response library.
Lead monthly security risk reviews.

Within the first 6 months:

Deliver SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 surveillance audits with no major nonconformances.
Complete an annual IEC 62443 security assessment of the product and track remediations.
Apply controls over Confidential Data with the IT Lead across our Corporate Environment.
Select and implement a Vulnerability Management tool to streamline detection, tracking and resolution across SCA, CSPM, SAST, DAST, and license compliance.
Conduct penetration tests of our cloud environment and physical sensor.
Plan and conduct a 3rd party incident response tabletop, and address findings.
Mature CrowdStrike detection rules and SIEM coverage.

Within the first year:

Propose a 2–3 year security roadmap that fulfills LineVision’s vision for security excellence, including tooling, budget, and resourcing as the company grows.
Reduce questionnaire effort per customer through self-service trust materials and a mature answer library.
Plan and conduct a purple team exercise against LineVision and address findings.
Define security requirements for next-generation sensors and platform features.
Establish ISMS efficacy metrics reported quarterly to leadership.
Lead quarterly Governance, Risk & Compliance reviews with executive leadership.

How to succeed in this role

Key Competencies

Ownership: take full responsibility for the security program's outcomes, from audit results to customer confidence.
Planning & Prioritization: absorb interrupt-driven work (questionnaires, incidents, audit requests) while keeping long-term projects on schedule, and raise a flag early when something must slip.
Communication: explain risk clearly to engineers, executives, customers, and auditors; tailor the message to the audience.
Judgment: make risk-based decisions that balance security with business velocity.
People Leadership: develop direct and cross-functional team members and delegate meaningful ownership rather than doing the work yourself.

Essential Skills

6+ years in information security, with at least 2 years in a lead or people-management role.
Direct ownership (not only support) of SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 audits.
Experience conducting risk assessments with NIST CSF or an equivalent framework.
Hands-on experience with penetration test management, vulnerability management, and EDR/SIEM tooling (CrowdStrike preferred).
Experience with AWS cloud security.
Experience responding to enterprise customer security questionnaires and contract requirements.
CISSP, or a commitment to earn it within 18 months of start date.

What Sets The Best Candidates Apart

Experience with OT/ICS or IoT security, including IEC 62443.
Familiarity with utility sector requirements (CEII, NERC CIP) or other regulated critical infrastructure.
Experience leading incident response for a real event.
Experience with Vanta or similar compliance automation.
Experience in AI Governance and/or assessing the security of AI tools and features.

Reporting & Team Structure

Reports to the VP of Security, IT & Quality.
Manages the Security Analyst.
Partners with the IT Lead on IT controls, identity, endpoint security, and CEII controls.
Partners with Platform, DevOps, and Hardware teams on vulnerability remediation, SDLC evidence, and disaster recovery.
Partners with Customer Success and Sales on customer security engagements, and with Legal on contract terms and incident response.

What does joining LineVision mean for you?

Impact. Your talent, time, and energy will critically impact our success in accelerating our mission of providing utilities with grid intelligence to enable affordable, reliable power.
Ownership. You will hold broad responsibilities with high autonomy and trust in a communicative, collaborative, and fast-paced environment.
Flexibility. You will be empowered to maintain work-life balance with trust-based PTO and a flexible work schedule.
Real World Innovation. You will join a motivated and high-performing team working with cutting edge, patented technology to help solve key obstacles to meet the demands of an AI-powered future.

Who we are…

LineVision is a grid-enhancing technology company enabling electric utilities to deliver affordable, reliable power and accelerate the electrification of the global economy. Our grid intelligence platform delivers the most accurate, network-wide dynamic line ratings and enables safer, more reliable grid operations with a combination of optical sensors and advanced environmental modeling. LineVision's global customer base includes eight of the ten largest US utilities, including National Grid, Southern Company, and Exelon.

We are LineVisionaries:

We are Innovators: We light the way with tenacious creativity and do good work.
We are Empowered: With high trust and high autonomy, the floor is yours, and the opportunity is ours.
We are Welcoming: Come as you are, our doors are open. We are better together.
We are Trusted Partners: We elevate our customer champions through shared thought leadership. We deliver on commitments.
We are All In: We are building a community of passionate individuals who want to dent the universe.

At LineVision there’s no such thing as a "perfect" candidate. We are looking for exceptional people who want to make a positive impact through their work and facilitate an organization where everyone can thrive. So whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this role would make you excited to come to work every day.

LineVision embraces AI, and we understand leveraging AI in your job search. As an actual member of LineVision's hiring team reviews every application, we kindly ask that any final materials you submit reflect your own voice and authentic human experience.

Message to applicants applying to work in the U.S.

The base salary range for this role is $140,000-180,000 USD. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, education, and other relevant qualifications. This role is also eligible to participate in a company bonus plan. Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements.

Spacecraft represent the most pressing unmet need across the entire aerospace industry. As more launch vehicles come online and the cost to orbit decreases, more companies launching payloads to space continue to emerge.

For the first time in history, this influx of payload companies combined with reduced launch costs has resulted in a massive increase in need for commercial spacecraft platforms, known as satellite buses. These buses hold the payloads of our customers and are flown on launch vehicles.

Apex manufactures these satellite buses at scale using a combination of software, vertical integration, and hardware that is designed for manufacturing. Our spacecraft enable the future of society: ranging from earth observation to communications and more.

We’d love for you to join us on our mission of providing humankind access to the galaxy beyond our planet.

About The Role

Apex is seeking an experienced Technical Project Manager with strong experience in cybersecurity to lead initiatives focused on Command and Control.

Responsibilities

Serve as the central point of coordination across Cyber, Product, and Engineering, helping define what each function owns and ensuring the three teams remain aligned
Own end-to-end delivery across C2 program workflows, coordinating complex, multi-team deployments and rollouts
Offload and manage the product set and requirements across teams
Build reporting processes to ensure effective team coordination
Lead planning and execution of programs tied to ATO accreditation
(FedRAMP) Help define and manage priorities between product, cyber, and engineering
Own day-to-day program management; Run regular status touchpoints and progress reporting across the three teams
Ensure documentation (requirements, program status, accreditation materials) stays current and accessible

Required Qualifications

Experience running technical programs across multiple functions (security/cyber, product, engineering, etc.) simultaneously
Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with comfortability making real-time calls on sprint priorities and trade-offs across teams
Excellent communication skills, with a strong ability to translate between technical, product, and compliance-oriented stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

Background in both program management and product management
Experience in cloud or C2 (command and control) program environments
Experience coordinating with third-party partners on technical or compliance requirements
Comfort operating with less deep systems/software engineering ownership and more cross-functional orchestration

Additional

Experience with ATO/accreditation processes (FedRAMP) strongly preferred

Why Join Apex?

Apex believes in creating a work environment that you look forward to embracing every day. Our employees love working at Apex, and we want you to love it too. We're a fast-growing startup that has raised more than $500M in funding, and we invest heavily in our people from day one.

What We Offer For Full-time Employees

Shared upside: Receive equity in Apex, letting you benefit from the work you create
Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision for you and your dependents, plus $100k life insurance at no cost
Comprehensive PTO package: Starting at 15 days vacation, growing to 20+ days annually, plus 10 paid holidays
Competitive 401(k) plan: Generous matching - 100% match on first 3%, 50% on next 2%
8 weeks paid parental leave: Plus childcare reimbursement up to $350/day for work-related travel
Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks: To keep you fueled throughout the day
Vibrant community: Monthly office socials, pickleball tournaments, run club, and gatherings for you and your family
Your dream desk setup: All the tools you need to be your most productive self
World-class Playa Vista office: With the benefit of in-person collaboration with amazing coworkers and flexibility to integrate work and life
Real impact opportunity: Work alongside experts from aerospace, new space, and other cutting-edge industries to make a lasting difference

Additional Information

Compensation ranges are set by role, level, location, and alignment with market data. A candidate's specific level and base pay are determined case by case and may vary with job-related skills, education, experience, technical capabilities, and internal equity. Beyond base salary, full-time hires are also eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options, along with medical, dental, and vision coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan.

Description

Job Summary:

The Program Manager provides comprehensive leadership and oversight of multiple government-contract projects and operational efforts, from requirements development and proposal support through execution, delivery, and closeout. This position is accountable for program performance, financial planning and execution, resource allocation, contract compliance, risk management, and the supervision of assigned personnel. The Program Manager serves as a primary interface among government customers, company leadership, technical and operational teams, contracting and finance personnel, subcontractors, and vendors to meet mission requirements while maintaining cost, schedule, quality, and contractual performance.

Job Functions

Lead and coordinate multiple concurrent projects and tasking efforts; translate customer requirements and statements of work into actionable plans, schedules, deliverables, staffing requirements, and execution priorities.
Develop and maintain project baselines, milestone schedules, work breakdowns, resource plans, action-item trackers, and other program management tools; identify dependencies and adjust plans as mission needs evolve.

jobs.description:
Description

Job Title: Strategic Operations Manager, AI

Reports To: Head of Learning.ai (UGHE, CTLT)

Location: University of Global Health Equity (UGHE), Rwanda

Purpose of the Job

Reporting to the Head of Learning.ai (UGHE, CTLT), the Strategic Operations Manager owns the measurement framework and reporting for the Learning.ai portfolio, including the OneSpaceAfrica (OSA) platform and the eLearning program. The role (i) defines and tracks the metrics that show whether OSA is working, including the quality, reliability, safety, and fairness of its AI-enabled features, (ii) builds the outcomes and evaluation framework used to report results to partners, including COMS-A, and to donors, and (iii) works with the team to turn OSA performance data into findings for academic publication. The role also contributes to the design of needs assessments across the COMS-A network.

Key Responsibilities

Own the Learning.ai measurement framework, defining the core metrics used to evaluate OSA and the broader portfolio, including engagement, efficacy, efficiency, and AI performance, and setting the targets the team is held to. This includes the outcomes used to assess AI quality, reliability, safety, bias and fairness, and human review effectiveness ;
Track progress against targets with the Head of Learning.ai and the Manager, Product & Engineering, holding the roadmap accountable to evidence without owning the roadmap itself ;
Define what AI and product outcomes need to be measured, and works with engineering so the platform captures the data evaluation requires. Product decisions, instrumentation, and the roadmap stay with the Product and Engineering team ;
Lead evaluation design for each funding phase, including primary and secondary outcomes, a baseline and comparator approach drawing on pilot usage and infrastructure data, implementation fidelity measures, adoption and usage thresholds, AI performance and safety measures, and the success thresholds that would justify further investment. C ontribute faculty time and cost metrics, including cost per site and cost per student, to funding proposals ;
Contribute to needs -assessment design , working with the Partner Success Coordinator on interview and survey instruments so that findings can feed the evaluation framework ;
Hire and manage the Phase 0 needs-assessment consultant(s) and the Senior Advisor, Metrics, Analytics, and AI Evaluation, and hold them to their terms of reference. Day-to-day direction of needs-assessment fieldwork sits with the Partner Success Coordinator ;
Design the data strategy for performance management , determining what the OSA platform captures directly and what comes from surveys, interviews, and other faculty and student input, first at UGHE and then across the COMS-A network ;
Co-own the data management plan with the Infrastructure and DevOps Engineer, covering de-identification, data deposit, and the ethics approval required before platform data is used for research ;
Lead reporting to partners, donors, and internal leadership , and set the guardrails for how OSA results are reported externally ;
Prepare OSA performance findings for academic publication , working with the team on analysis and write-up ;
Work with external advisors , CTLT, COMS-A, and PIH's monitoring and evaluation team to ground Learning.ai's measurement approach in established practice.

Key Deliverables

Approved Learning.ai measurement framework, with defined metrics, targets, and AI quality, reliability, safety, and fairness measures
Evaluation design for each funding phase, including baseline, comparator, and success thresholds
Data strategy and data management plan in place, with ethics approval secured before platform data is used for research
Timely and accurate reporting to partners, donors, and internal leadership
OSA performance findings prepared for academic publication

Qualifications, Knowledge, And Skills

Academic qualifications
Bachelor’s degree required in a quantitative or research-oriented field (e.g., Statistics, Economics, Public Health, Social Science, Data Science, or Business); master’s degree preferred
Experience
Experience designing or managing program evaluation, M&E, or impact measurement; experience in education, global health, or international development preferred
Experience measuring or evaluating digital or AI-enabled systems, including the ability to work with technical and domain experts to define meaningful measures of quality, reliability, safety, and fairness
Experience with research design and ethics review, including baselines, comparators, and governance of personal data
Project management experience, including scoping work and managing external consultants
Technical competencies
Strong quantitative skills, with experience defining metrics, building reporting, and turning data into recommendations for decision-makers
Comfortable working with product and engineering teams to define what data needs to be captured and how
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English; English proficiency required
French and/or Kinyarwanda proficiency preferred
Behavioral competencies
Ability to work effectively in a team in a complex, fast-paced environment
Exceptional interpersonal skills, including the ability to interact professionally with culturally diverse staff, partners, and clients
Flexibility and agility
Passion for social justice and global health

How to Apply

Applicants should provide: (1) curriculum vitae, (2) degree, (3) a cover letter describing your interest in UGHE and relevant experience. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page.

University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Organizational Profile

UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system.

UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima—PIH’s sister organization—and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade.

Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team.

Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment

At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work—including community members—as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy.

UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
Accurx is where conversations happen with and about patients in the NHS

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. At Accurx, we’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that connects everyone through communication.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient, has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices and 68% (and growing!) of NHS Trusts.

Our platform now powers Total Triage
to manage patient demand, and Self-Book
that lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires
for long-term conditions, while Accumail
finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe
,
our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.

We’re not just shipping features. We’re giving clinicians their time back and ensuring every patient journey is as smooth as it should be.

Gamechanging, right? Here's what you'll be getting stuck into to make it work

As an Implementation Manager,
you’ll be the one making sure our most ambitious tools actually land and stick in Secondary care. You won't just be ticking boxes on a rollout list; you’ll be leading the charge on high-impact transformations, like helping clinicians and admin teams move over to Accurx Scribe
.
You'll spend your time figuring out how these tools fit into the daily lives of clinicians, making sure they aren't just "installed," but are genuinely making things better for everyone.

Driving deep transformation: Leading big-scale rollouts for complex products like Scribe, making sure we’re not just doing the basics but fundamentally changing how healthcare is delivered.
Strategic boundary-setting: Standing firm on implementation plans and managing commercial expectations to ensure we deliver sustainable solutions without overcommitting.
Owning the AI journey: Becoming the go-to expert on our emerging AI features, taking full ownership of how they are introduced to practices and scaled across the country.
Closing the feedback loop: Reviewing practice cohorts 6-9 months after go-live to see if they’re actually using the product as intended and figuring out how we can make it even better.
Scaling with smarts: Using our internal AI dashboards to handle the "heavy lifting" of data, so you can focus on the human side of implementation while we automate the repetitive bits.
Raising the bar: Constantly looking for ways to improve our processes—if something isn't working or could be more efficient, you’ll have the autonomy to change it.

You should apply if...

You’ve been around the block with big rollouts: You have solid experience managing complex implementations in a fast-paced business and you know how to keep a project moving.
You’re a "driver," not a "passenger": You don't wait to be told what to do; you dive into the context, spot the problems, and take the lead on solving them.
You can hold your own: You’re comfortable having tough conversations with stakeholders and can stay firm on what’s achievable
You’re a natural communicator: You can explain technical or complex changes in a way that feels clear, simple, and actually exciting for the people using them.
You’re relentlessly resourceful: When you hit a roadblock, you don't just stop - you find a creative way over, under, or through it.
You care about the "why": You’re motivated by the idea of fixing healthcare communication and want to see the real-world impact of your work on clinicians and patients.

What’s in it for you?

You’ll join a high-performing team on a mission to solve healthcare productivity, building a platform used by around 300k NHS staff every week, supporting the care of over 50 million NHS patients every year. We set a high bar, move fast, and give people the ownership and support to do the best work of their careers

£45,000 - £60,000 salary, plus a discretionary recognition bonus for exceptional performance and impact, nominated by managers and awarded by our leadership team
Equity: £15,000 in equal share options, so you share in the value you help create
Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life
Built for collaboration: We are an office-first culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office for a minimum of 3 days a week
Close to our users: Regular hackathons, plus dedicated time to visit GP practices and other healthcare settings to see first-hand how our products are used
Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year
Support at home: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support
We have our very own chefs: Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches, plus a weekly sweet treat

Job Description

The Opportunity

OCI is evolving the application and infrastructure deployment capabilities that help engineering teams deliver regular, reliable code updates to production. Our change-management and release-management tooling provides the workflows, controls, and operational visibility needed to move services forward while maintaining the highest standards of production stability.

As a Technical Program Manager, you will coordinate delivery of these core platform capabilities across engineering teams. You will bring structure to complex release dependencies, help teams translate operational needs into clear plans, and support the safe adoption of automation that improves deployment frequency, reduces manual effort, and protects production reliability.

What We Are Looking For

Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

3+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering operations, release engineering, product operations, or a related role in a technical environment.
Experience supporting application deployment, infrastructure automation, CI CD, release engineering, cloud infrastructure, or comparable platform programs.
Ability to work effectively with technical teams and understand deployment workflows, change-management controls, release dependencies, production risk, and operational tradeoffs.
Demonstrated ability to create clear plans, manage milestones and actions, communicate status, and bring stakeholders together to resolve delivery and operational issues.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with care for precise documentation, release readiness, and consistent follow-through.
A collaborative, customer-oriented, and data-informed approach to improving software delivery, change management, and production stability.

Preferred qualifications:
Experience in one or more of the following areas is a plus.

Application deployment platforms, continuous delivery, release management, change management, or deployment orchestration.
Infrastructure-as-code, GitOps, cloud infrastructure automation, configuration management, or infrastructure deployment.
CI CD, source control, build and test automation, artifact management, release engineering, or workflow orchestration.
Site reliability engineering, incident response, observability, production readiness, software supply-chain controls, or compliance automation.
OCI services or comparable large-scale public cloud environments.

Why This Role

You will help define how OCI engineering teams safely deliver change to production. The programs and tooling you support will enable more frequent code updates, reduce release friction, and help maintain the stability and operational confidence that critical cloud services require.

About OCI

Oracle Cloud Infrastructure delivers cloud services for organizations worldwide. The OCI Developer Platform team creates the capabilities that help engineering organizations build, deploy, and operate software with speed, confidence, and control.

Responsibilities

What You Will Do

Coordinate programs that deliver application and infrastructure deployment capabilities, automated change management, and release-management tooling used across OCI.
Work with engineering, product, SRE, security, compliance, and operations partners to define milestones, dependencies, readiness criteria, and success measures for production changes.
Support the design, delivery, and adoption of automated deployment and change workflows that provide appropriate approvals, policy controls, auditability, and rollback paths.
Drive initiatives that enable frequent, predictable production code refreshes while reducing manual release work, deployment friction, and operational risk.
Track execution across teams, identify release risks and blockers early, and coordinate timely decisions, escalation, and follow-through through rollout.
Use operational signals such as deployment success rates, change failure rates, lead time, rollback frequency, and incident data to assess program health and prioritize improvements.
Communicate release readiness, risks, dependencies, and recommended actions clearly to stakeholders across the engineering organization.

jobs.description:
Join us as a FinCrime Data Analyst Lead at Barclays, where you will act as the Data Analytics Lead for Financial Crime Agile Testing. You will oversee data analytics work performed within the Agile Testing team and define the analytical testing approach for individual reviews. Working in partnership with Agile Testing colleagues, you will translate review triggers into executable objectives, hypotheses and data analytics testing plans, provide input to review scope, and determine data requirements and analytical design. You will quality-control analytical scripts and outputs, communicate data-led findings and observations to stakeholders, and act as the escalation route for Data Analytics Specialists and Analysts. Through independent judgement, technical assurance and constructive challenge, you will help deliver timely, risk-based and hypothesis-led testing of Financial Crime processes and controls.

Purpose of the Role

To oversee and lead the data analytics work supporting Financial Crime Agile Testing reviews. The role determines the overall data analytics approach, defines executable analytical objectives, hypotheses and testing plans for individual reviews, provides quality control over analytical scripts and outputs, and translates data into testable insight that supports assessment of the operational effectiveness of Financial Crime controls.

Key Accountabilities

Oversee data analytics work performed within the Financial Crime Agile Testing team, including defining the data analytics testing strategy required for individual reviews.
Translate review triggers into executable objectives, hypotheses and data analytics testing plans, providing data-led input to scoping decisions in collaboration with non-Data Analytics review colleagues.
Provide leadership and technical oversight for the development of analytical test objectives, methodologies and scripts using SQL, Python and SAS; review and approve analytical work to support robust and reproducible testing outcomes.
Identify and agree data needs and analytical design with the Agile Testing Lead during review planning and test-plan development.
Coordinate delivery of analytics with the Agile Testing Lead during testing execution, while Data Analytics Specialists and Analysts design scripts, source data and perform analysis.
Perform quality-control reviews of analytical scripts, including SQL, SAS and Python, designed by Data Analytics Specialists and/or Data Analytics Analysts, challenging logic, assumptions, data quality, caveats and the sufficiency of analytical evidence.
Review analytical outputs and workpaper content to support clear, accurate and reproducible documentation of the testing performed, evidence obtained and conclusions supported by the analysis.
Interpret and communicate findings and observations arising from data analytics testing to external stakeholders and provide analytical insight and draft input to review conclusions and reporting.
Act as the escalation route for Data Analytics Specialists and Analysts, addressing analytical judgement matters within authority and escalating material risk, scope, timeline or stakeholder issues where appropriate.
Work alongside the Agile Testing Lead as part of stage-gate oversight and peer cross-review, preserving independent challenge and clear accountability between Testing and Data Analytics roles.
Support the ongoing review and improvement of data analytics requirements within the Agile Testing methodology and contribute to efficient, risk-based and hypothesis-led review delivery.
Maintain independence and objectivity, ensure timely escalation, secure evidence retention, data-privacy compliance and high-quality documentation across data analytics work.

Stakeholder Management and Leadership

The role requires strong engagement across business teams and larger FinCrime Agile testing team. The VP determines the overall data analytics approach and analytical scoping decisions for individual reviews. The role exercises independent judgement when setting analytical hypotheses and approaches, reviews work completed by Data Analytics Specialists and Analysts, and acts as their escalation route. The role also contributes to the strategic development of the Financial Crime Agile Testing analytics capability and adoption of improved tools and techniques

Basic / Essential Qualifications

Strong experience leading data analytics work in Financial Crime, Compliance, Risk, Audit, Assurance or another control-testing environment.
Strong SQL and Python capability, including the ability to review and challenge analytical scripts, logic, assumptions and outputs developed by others.
Experience translating risk or review triggers into analytical objectives, hypotheses, testing plans, data requirements and executable analytical approaches.
Strong understanding of Financial Crime processes, risks and controls across relevant domains such as AML, Sanctions, Customer Due Diligence/KYC, Fraud or Transaction Monitoring.
Experience applying data analytics to assess control effectiveness using full-population or targeted testing approaches.
Strong technical assurance, critical-thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify data-quality issues, anomalies, control weaknesses, caveats and limitations.
Experience reviewing analytical evidence and workpapers to determine whether testing outputs sufficiently support observations and conclusions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain analytical findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Strong stakeholder engagement, collaboration and constructive-challenge skills, with the ability to exercise independent judgement and escalate appropriately.
Ability to coordinate analytical delivery, provide technical guidance and act as an escalation point for Data Analytics Specialists and Analysts.

Desirable Skillsets

Experience contributing to Financial Crime assurance or Agile Testing methodology and improving analytical testing standards or ways of working.
Experience with SAS, data visualisation tools such as Tableau, statistical analysis, data mining or AI-enabled analytics.
Experience developing reusable analytical assets or automated testing approaches that improve testing efficiency, consistency or coverage.
Knowledge of advanced statistical or machine-learning techniques used to identify patterns, trends and relationships in data.
Working knowledge of AWS cloud services, LLM architectures, including responsible AI principles and appropriate solution validation.

You may be assessed on key critical skills relevant for success in the role, including technical assurance, critical thinking, Financial Crime risk and control analysis, root-cause analysis, systems proficiency, stakeholder engagement, collaboration and data analytics using SQL and Python, as well as job-specific skillsets.

Role is based out of Pune.

Purpose of the role

To enable data-driven strategic and operational decision making through extracting actionable insights from large datasets, performing statistical and advanced analytics to uncover trends and patterns, and presenting findings through clear visualisations and reports.

Accountabilities

Investigation and analysis of data issues related to quality, lineage, controls, and authoritative source identification, documenting data sources, methodologies, and quality findings with recommendations for improvement
Designing and building data pipelines to automate data movement and processing.
Apply advanced analytical techniques to large datasets to uncover trends and correlations, develop validated logical data models, and translate insights into actionable business recommendations that drive operational and process improvements, leveraging machine learning/AI.
Through data-driven analysis, translate analytical findings into actionable business recommendations, identifying opportunities for operational and process improvements.

CrowdStrike is a fast-growing cybersecurity company that protects customers from breaches. You will establish the operational foundation for new projects, coordinating project setup, initial financial requirements, stakeholder alignment, documentation, risk management, and kickoff planning. Working across a matrixed organization, you will clarify ownership, resolve readiness gaps, and coordinate a structured transition from pursuit to delivery.

By developing a consistent, scalable mobilization approach, you will help reduce startup delays, strengthen accountability, protect early project performance, and enable delivery teams to begin execution promptly upon award.

Assess mobilization requirements for new awards and contract modifications, tailoring the approach to the scope, complexity, and delivery impact of the change.

Coordinate project code creation and initial financial setup with Finance and other stakeholders, securing required approvals at the appropriate stage.

Identify, document, and track key risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies, and decisions; escalate gaps that could affect launch readiness or early performance.
Develop the initial kickoff and transition plan, including meeting cadence, communications, required documentation, and handoff expectations.
Facilitate readiness reviews and cross-functional working sessions to resolve outstanding actions and confirm preparedness for project launch.
Coordinate the transition to delivery leadership, confirming ownership and acceptance of startup documentation, open actions, and ongoing responsibilities.
Track mobilization progress, communicate status to leadership, and incorporate lessons learned into reusable templates, tools, and processes.
Close mobilization after agreed exit criteria are met and remaining actions and responsibilities have been formally transferred.

Executive presence and communication skills
Attention to detail with strong organizational skills
Project mobilization and planning: Ability to translate evolving pursuit information into practical startup plans, milestones, and readiness criteria.
Cross-functional leadership and influence: Ability to align teams and drive accountability within a matrixed organization.
Operational and financial coordination: Understanding of project setup, financial dependencies, and the controls needed to support timely execution.
Risk management and problem-solving: Ability to anticipate startup barriers, evaluate dependencies, and resolve or escalate issues promptly.
Communication and stakeholder management: Clear, concise communication with sales, program leaders, delivery teams, and executive stakeholders.
Process improvement and organization: Ability to create repeatable practices, maintain accurate documentation, and manage competing priorities.

Experience developing project plans, tracking risks and dependencies, maintaining project documentation, and communicating progress to leadership.
Strong organizational, analytical, negotiation, and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and work effectively through ambiguity.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
new_jobs.description:
The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
will partner with senior leaders across Development and Alumni Relations (DAR) to translate research insights into strategic recommendations for OPG and OFR staff, faculty and academic leadership, and other DAR colleagues, informing the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of prospective UHNW individual and foundation donors to Johns Hopkins University and Medicine.

Reporting to the Office of Principal Gifts (OPG) with a dotted line to Prospect Research within the Office of Advancement Services (OAS), this position will be matrixed to support the Office of Foundation Relations (OFR), with a focus on prospective ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals, foundations, family offices, financial institutions, and other key philanthropic partners. This individual will possess deep subject matter expertise in foundation research, wealth screenings, relationship mapping, and due diligence best practices.

The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst is responsible for partnering with the Office of Principal Gifts to implement and lead a comprehensive program of prospect identification, prospect analysis, and prospect monitoring. The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will conduct and advise others that are conducting research and ensure that the research meets the highest standards of confidentiality, quality, accuracy, and timeliness along with utmost attention to detail.

The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will apply, and model for others, excellent research, writing, presentation and organizational skills and implements new ways to secure and analyze information and leverage existing relationships to make connections to high-net-worth potential prospects. The Sr. Prospect Research and Intelligence Analyst will work independently as well as collaboratively as a senior/lead member of the team.

Specific Duties & Responsibilities

Portfolio and Pipeline Management

Support portfolio reviews through partnerships with Development Research. This includes providing key information about managed prospects to support portfolio management and strategy discussions, in addition to capturing relevant data in the CRM.

Relationship Management Reporting

Generate reports that provide accurate projections of gifts in the pipeline and snapshots of the prospect pool and strategies. This will require the ability to query and compile CRM data for portfolio and pipeline projects as well as monthly, quarterly, and annual office reports.

Orient and Train Colleagues

Serve as the key trainer and technical support for DAR staff, supporting fundraisers across all business units. This includes disseminating and communicating changes in business practices (as needed) to administrative staff, documenting standard operating procedures, coordinating training schedules, and managing user roles in the CRM for incoming and outgoing DAR staff.

Build Internal Relationships

Develop and maintain effective work relationships with various colleagues and work as an effective RMPA team member. This includes responding to routine requests for information, providing answers to problems and/or inquiries relating to donors and prospects, and collaborating with gift officers to solicit input and explain database decisions.
Identify and cultivate key relationships within the Office of Advancement Services that enable the efficient execution of essential tasks to support data integrity and reporting.

Other duties as assigned.

In addition to the duties listed above, the Sr. Prospect and Intelligence Analyst, Principal Gifts
will:

Proactively identify new UHNW individual and foundation prospects with transformational giving capacity, using existing database resources and fee-based tools. Apply relationship mapping tools to evaluate Johns Hopkins connections to priority UHNW individuals, senior program officers and foundation leaders, family offices, corporations, funding collaboratives, and other philanthropic and wealth management entities.
Present research findings in concise, strategic, and actionable formats for senior university leadership and fundraising staff across the institution, supported by deep subject matter expertise in foundation philanthropy and trends in UHNW individual giving.
Partner with OFR and OPG colleagues to advance the institution’s hybrid foundations model, ensuring a coordinated approach to UHNW individual and foundation strategies. Lead projects that identify new alignments between funders and university priorities, and opportunities to deepen existing relationships, elevating high-potential findings to the appropriate university and medicine partners.
Identify founders, executives, investors, and entrepreneurs associated with companies approaching IPOs, acquisitions, or other significant liquidity events, so Hopkins can build authentic relationships before wealth events occur rather than approaching prospects afterward.
Proactively track, analyze, and disseminate relevant financial and market trends impacting the institutions top donors and prospects, including stock performance, company valuations and IPOs, foundation asset evaluations, and shifts in donor-advised fund management.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
Five years related experience with a minimum of two years direct prospect research experience.
Additional education may substitute for required experience and additional related experience may substitute for required education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.

Preferred Qualifications

Seven years of related work experience.
Demonstrated track record of strategic and creative approaches to research and collaboration with frontline fundraisers, system administrators, and senior level management preferred.
Expertise in research and analytical methods, including proficiency in advanced online search strategies, complex database use, and familiarity with research tools such as Salesforce, iWave, LexisNexis, Wealth-X, Altrata, and other screening tools.
Ability and willingness to understand the business of fundraising and how data insights can inform and drive decisions.
Ability to evaluate and pilot new tools, technologies, and data presentation formats that enhance strategic decision-making, including AI-enabled tools, using prompt engineering and large language model (LLM) queries to accelerate prospect research, synthesize information, and surface insights.
Proficiency of the prospect research competencies and best practices presented through the Association of Professional Researchers for Advancement (APRA) Body of Knowledge and relevant development tools.

You'll be part of an AI-native company. We're rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.
You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.
You'll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Business Operations Manager to be a force multiplier for our BizOps Director: someone who can take an ambiguous, cross-functional problem, build the trust to step into another team's operations, and drive a data-driven fix.

You'll own cross-functional projects end to end, scoping them, driving implementation, and measuring success. You'll partner directly with functional leaders (Sales, Dealer Success, Ops) to diagnose operational challenges and help fix them.

What You'll Own

Cross-Functional Project Ownership

Lead cross-functional initiatives from scoping through execution.
Drive accountability across teams you don't formally manage. Keep initiatives moving, surface risks early, and make sure deliverables ship.
Take on problems that arrive as symptoms ("this handoff keeps breaking," "onboarding is too slow") and figure out what's actually going on to propose a fix.

Operational Partnership

Partner directly with functional leaders to diagnose inefficiencies in how their teams operate.
Analyze data to size a problem and diagnose the root cause.
Design and implement fixes such as new agentic workflows, automations, and SOPs.
Lead and facilitate department operations, such as weekly business reviews.
Act on diagnosed daily metric alerts.

What You'll Bring

4-7 years of experience in business operations, strategy and operations, consulting, or a high-growth startup operations role. Marketplace or automotive experience is a plus.
A track record of owning ambiguous problems end-to-end.
Strong stakeholder management: you can walk into a team you don't manage, build credibility fast, and drive change without formal authority.
Comfortable with data (SQL a plus) and analytics.
Excellent written and verbal communication. A structured thinker who can bring clarity to a messy situation.
Bias toward action, low ego, and thrives in zero-to-one ambiguity.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Carollo Engineers is a leading engineering firm dedicated exclusively to water. For over 90 years, we've specialized in the planning, design, and construction of water, wastewater, stormwater, and reuse facilities, bringing innovative and sustainable solutions to the water sector's most complex challenges.

We work with water agencies, municipalities, utilities, research organizations, and private companies across various industries, including technology, manufacturing, and beyond. These clients choose Carollo because we employ some of the most knowledgeable and experienced professionals in the world. When you join our team, you'll work alongside industry leaders who are advancing the science of water, protecting public health, and building resilient communities.

Carollo's vision is to be the best water consulting firm and the best place for you to build your career. If you're passionate about making a difference in this critical field, we invite you to explore a career with Carollo.

Responsibilities

Expand Carollo’s presence in the local stormwater market via targeted business development strategies, including growing specific client relationships and participating in select professional society activities.
Collaborate with the Stormwater Leads across the company to develop/implement strategy for continued stormwater growth and innovation across the company.
Manage planning and detailed design projects, including management of contract document production (i.e., plan sets and specifications), hydraulic and hydrologic calculations, report writing, and other activities needed to support the planning, design, and construction services for stormwater management facilities. Project may include pipelines, open channels, pump stations, channel stabilization, storage and treatment facilities, multi-benefit facilities, and other conveyance measures.
Collaborate with other engineering disciplines, designers, and scientists, among others, who support specific assignments.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Civil, Environmental, or Agricultural Engineering or other appropriate engineering major
10+ years of experience relating to stormwater and water resources projects
Minimum 5 years of experience managing a team to deliver planning and design solutions for urban stormwater management challenges.
Minimum 5 years of experience with client service and business development efforts, including project positioning, proposal preparation, interviews, and technical presentations
Familiarity with standard stormwater analysis tools, including HEC-RAS (1D/2D), HEC-HMS, ICM, FLO-2D, XPSWMM, ArcGIS, and Civil 3D.
Experience with the selection and optimization of multi-benefit urban storm water projects
Strong verbal and written communication skills
Strong team building skills
Ability to apply critical thinking
Ability to present to groups and communicate effectively with clients and project team
Proficiency in MS Word, Outlook, Excel, and PowerPoint

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Civil, Environmental, or Agricultural Engineering or other appropriate engineering major
Experience with FEMA floodplain delineation and submittal of Letters of Map Revision and Conditional Letters of Map Revision

Compensation Range

$140,000 to $190,000 annually. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we

would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the

posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee’s pay within the salary

range will be based on several factors including, but limited to, relevant education, qualifications,

certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or

organizational needs.

Other Compensation And Benefits

Carollo is committed to providing employees with a competitive, comprehensive benefits program that provides the support employees and their families need to lead healthy, productive lives. Carollo’s benefits package includes paid time off and holidays, comprehensive health insurance coverage, pre-tax savings account options for healthcare, dependent care and commuter expenses, disability insurance and life insurance options for you and your dependents. We also offer free Caregiver Support, Travel Assistance, counseling services, discount programs, and a Lifestyle Reimbursement Account. Other compensation that may be available includes: 401(k) company contribution matching, tuition reimbursement, discretionary bonuses, career advancement bonuses, professional registration bonuses, employee referral bonuses, and compensatory time for exempt employees. new_jobs.description:
About This Role

We're looking for a curious, detail-oriented Data Analyst to join our growing Data & Analytics team. This is a true generalist role: you'll be a go-to partner across the company, supporting Retail, Wholesale, Ecommerce, Marketing, and beyond with the reporting and insights they need to make smarter decisions.

One day you might be building a sales report for our store teams, the next you're digging into wholesale account performance or helping Marketing understand what's driving results. You'll work with data from every corner of the business, which means you'll see how it all connects and have a real hand in shaping where we go next.

You'll join a small, forward-thinking team that's rethinking the role of data at Brighton. Your work will be visible, your ideas will be heard, and you'll have plenty of room to grow. If you love variety, enjoy solving problems, and want to see your analysis make an impact, we'd love to meet you.

This role reports to the Head of Data & Analytics.

Primary Responsibilities

Build and own reporting for our retail stores, wholesale accounts, ecommerce, and marketing teams
Analyze sales, customer, and channel performance to spot trends and opportunities
Forecast results and measure the impact of campaigns, initiatives, and business changes
Support customer data work including segmentation, data hygiene, and CRM and loyalty analytics
Partner with stakeholders across the company to answer questions and build scalable data solutions
Turn complex findings into clear, actionable stories for non-technical audiences

Here's What You'll Bring

2-3 years of experience in a data-focused or technical application support role
Strong SQL skills (any variant)
Proficiency in at least one of Python, JavaScript, PHP, or .NET
Expert Excel skills, including pivot tables and lookups
Sharp attention to detail and a commitment to accurate, trustworthy data
The ability to explain findings clearly to both technical and non-technical teams
A root-cause mindset: you ask "why," establish the facts, and understand the problem before proposing solutions
Strong problem-solving skills and the follow-through to take solutions from idea to done
Ownership of your work and a focus on results that move the business forward
Comfort juggling multiple priorities and deadlines with minimal supervision
Natural curiosity and a drive to answer questions with data

We'd Love If You Also Have

Experience with BI tools (Looker, Sigma, Tableau, Mode, Metabase)
Background in retail, wholesale, or omnichannel data (POS, sell-through, inventory)
Experience with CRM, CDP, or ESP platforms (Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Klaviyo, Braze, Segment)
Familiarity with A/B testing or incrementality measurement
Working knowledge of CCPA/CPRA and customer data privacy

We offer

Competitive salary and incentives
Inclusive benefits package including 401(k), medical, dental, and vision
Generous paid time off
Professional development and growth opportunities
Collaborative and innovative work environment

About Brighton

In 1972, our founders Jerry and Terri Kohl set out with a simple but bold idea: create beautifully crafted accessories that feel personal, meaningful, and made to last. They believed that artistry matters and that customers should be treated like lifelong friends. That belief still fuels us today.

At Brighton's headquarters, you'll find a community of passionate creators, problem-solvers, and innovators. Our buying team imagines what's next, our account specialists and shipping experts keep our nationwide network moving with precision, and our in-house artisans bring each design to life with extraordinary skill. We even have dedicated teams who restore and refresh beloved pieces so they can continue their journey with the people who cherish them.

Joining us means stepping into a place where heritage craftsmanship meets forward-thinking design. We're a company grounded in heart, yet always reaching for what's possible. Here, you're not just part of a brand, you're part of building the future of retail, one thoughtfully crafted handbag, necklace, and charm at a time.

new_jobs.title: Digital Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Viget is an independent digital agency that has been designing and building digital products and platforms since 1999. Our culture is ideal for lifelong learners seeking a variety of meaningful work, supportive collaboration with positive teammates, and a healthy work/life balance. We work from four offices (hybrid) and remote locations throughout the U.S., and enjoy a proven cadence of virtual and in-person meetings and retreats to build camaraderie and stay connected. We work with tech companies (like Robinhood and SpectrumAi), non-profits (like World Wildlife Fund and NPF), and consumer brands (like Stern Pinball and ESPN).

At Viget, Digital Project Managers are much more than just project coordinators -- they’re project leaders and lead consultants. They work collaboratively with clients to understand organization goals, define solutions, answer hard questions, and ensure the overall quality of a project. They facilitate tasking, budget management, and day-to-day communication with clients and internal teams. They are both empathetic and results-driven, cultivating a culture of efficiency, innovation, trust, and progress on their projects.

As a DPM at Viget, you’ll lead a variety of projects, including large-scale content sites, product design, and software development efforts. You’ll define and prioritize requirements, collaborate with our brilliant designers and developers, support user research and testing, lead quality assurance, and celebrate thrilling launches. More than any other role at Viget, you’ll contribute to all areas of a successful project.

You'll need to communicate, collaborate, and lead effectively. Here are the things we're looking for:

You’re a polished and persuasive communicator (without BS-ing). You consistently listen, make connections, write, and speak better than most people.
You were born with or have carefully cultivated an awareness of and appreciation for details.
You get made fun of by your friends because you’re “too” organized (as if THAT’S possible).
You meet deadlines across multiple, simultaneous projects.
You build long-term relationships with clients based on thorough planning, timely and professional communication, and intelligent problem-solving.
You’re solution-oriented. You don’t just identify problems, you synthesize solutions.
You’re comfortable closely managing project budgets. You can work with internal teams to manage their time within constraints, transparently communicate budget health to clients, and lead prioritization discussions to help clients understand tradeoffs and collaboratively identify solutions that work with their timelines and budgets.
You have a "thick skin" when the going gets tough. If and when conflicting demands emerge, you communicate diplomatically to reach a resolution.
You demonstrate integrity through your words and actions.
You love processes and plans, but you’re flexible. You can create an effective project plan and timeline, but are comfortable enough with ambiguity to adapt the plan when things change.

You'll also need to be able to work well in our technical environment. Here are things we’re looking for (note: we recognize that you may not have done all of these before, and that's okay):

You have worked in a fast-paced software development environment before, whether at an agency or product company.
You know how the web works and how a web app works, which means you’re aware of technical constraints when talking to clients. You don’t hesitate to ask a lot of questions in order to define the functionality of what we’re building.
You can break down a set of wireframes into actionable tasks for back-end and front-end developers. You’re passionate about finding innovative, efficient, and effective ways to document those tasks.
You can shepherd often-vague client requests and ideas through the definition process. You know when to rely on a UX designer, but you’re comfortable thinking through logic and creating useful documentation of that logic.
You’re able to describe workflows and tasks purely from an end user’s perspective, helping developers make informed implementation decisions.
You’ve performed QA. You can distinguish a bug from a functional update from a new feature request.
Generally, successful candidates will have between 3 and 8 years of experience managing digital projects. If the role has piqued your interest and you think you’d be a fit, but don’t quite meet the requirements, we still encourage you to reach out.

Everyone At Viget

Embodies our core values of integrity, work ethic, collaboration, creativity, and lifelong learning.
Values mentorship, learning, and sharing knowledge.
Writes and speaks clearly and effectively when collaborating with teammates and clients.
Believes in and supports our commitment to building a diverse and inclusive company.

Compensation And Benefits

Annual base salary of $70,000 - $100,000 (mid level) or $90,000 - $120,000 (senior) per year depending on location, skills, and experience
Additional comp available via spot performance bonuses, sales referrals, and new hire referrals
401(k) retirement plan matching up to 4%
100% company-paid health and dental coverage for you and your family
Stipends for wellness (apps, gyms, etc.) and connectivity (mobile phone or home internet)
15 days PTO (20 after 2 years), 9 paid holidays, and 2 community service days per year
Up to $2,000/year in conference and training (professional development) budget

How To Apply

Apply by completing the application form. We expect you may use AI for research, prep, and proofreading during the job application process. We use AI daily and believe that building AI skills is essential, but at this stage we need to get to know you
. To that end, unless directed otherwise, we expect you will not submit AI-generated answers or assignments (writing, coding, designing) nor use AI for real-time help during interviews. Using AI tools to misrepresent your knowledge, ability, or experience is unethical. It’s also impractical and short-sighted since once you’re in the role you’ll often need to think and communicate in real-time without AI help. As a small team with high standards for quality and, above all, integrity, we ask that you write your own application answers, submit work that reflects the real you, and share openly how you used AI in the application process if at all.

We encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet 100% of the qualifications and are actively seeking people from underrepresented groups to join our team.

Before you apply, learn more about us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Flickr, X, Vimeo, and by exploring pointlesscorp.com.

Viget maintains a drug-free workplace. We are unable to offer work visa sponsorship at this time.

Viget is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace where all of us feel valued and heard. new_jobs.title: Supply Chain Transfer Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Introduction to the job

Over the past decades, ASML has grown exponentially, and as we rely heavily on our supply chain, so has our supply chain ecosystem. In the coming years we expect further growth that will require a transformation of large parts of our Supply Chain. In order to tackle this strategic challenge and help Shape & Drive the transformation in our supply chain we created the ‘Supply Chain Transformation’ department within Strategic Sourcing & Procurement. From this department, a team of professionals in Supply Chain management disciplines will drive engagements / change programs in our supply chain and be supported with specific competencies from across ASML.

As a Supply Chain Transfer Manager, you will lead cross-functional teams responsible for managing critical supply chain transfers. Your goal is to ensure the timely and reliable availability of materials, working closely with stakeholders across technical and operational disciplines. You’ll drive project progress, safeguard supply continuity, and play a key role in managing transitions in our supply chain.

Role and responsibilities

The Supply Transfer Manger is responsible for:

Lead and manage {{b}}complex, multidisciplinary technical supply chain transfer projects{{/b}} from initial planning through execution, stabilization, and closure.
Develop and maintain {{b}}integrated project plans, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, critical paths, and risk mitigation actions{{/b}} to ensure transfers remain on schedule.
Lead cross-sector alignment on {{b}}technical test, qualification, and release requirements{{/b}} throughout the transfer, ensuring dependencies, risks, and readiness criteria are understood and managed across engineering, quality, supply chain, and supplier teams.
Identify gaps in technical documentation, requirements, and transfer readiness; own the documentation process and drive cross-functional teams to resolve gaps, clarify requirements, and achieve timely closure.
Manage the complexity of evolving technology and changing technical requirements that may impact product transfer scope, timing, and execution, proactively assessing dependencies and adjusting transfer plans to maintain continuity and project objectives.
Manage and lead multidisciplinary technical orientated cross-sector transfer team
Establish clear project governance and align with internal and external stakeholders on goals and plans
Collaborating to create and maintain the transfer portfolio
Supporting resource planning to ensure successful transfer execution
Set up a full phasing out/transfer product overview including (non) transfer, including
Capacity alignment across n-tier supply chain
Logistic risk mitigation such as buffer strategy and last buy decisions
Definition of technical release procedure per product category with transfer team and execute these
Solid input on phasing out negotiations to the Sourcing team
Proactively execute supply chain risk analysis and execute action plans to mitigate risk; ensuring Material availability at all phases of the program and right quality before and after shipment / ensuring on time delivery during the project
Manage escalations within transfers to solve bottlenecks in supply chain and avoid re-occurrence

Education and experience

Degree in engineering or related technical field. Master’s highly preferred.
10+ years relevant professional experience in a high-tech NPI environment.
Strong background in industrialization, supply chain, or sourcing.
Proven expertise in project management and familiarity with re-allocating products or production
Experience collaborating in cross-functional, technical environments to drive supply chain improvements
Experience directly managing suppliers and building trusting relationships
Risk management experience and business continuity

Skills

Familiarity with key technical concepts and technical understanding to engage effectively with engineering teams
Stakeholder Alignment & Decision Making
Project Governance
Portfolio Management
Strategic Sourcing Collaboration
Transfer Negotiation Support
Business Continuity Planning
Risk Mitigation Strategy Development
Excellent stakeholder management and relationship building skills
Conceptual thinker on strategic level
Strong analytical skills
Convincing / negotiation skills
Pragmatic and result driven
Pro-active attitude, drive for improvement

Other information

To be effective as Supply Transfer Manager requires close cooperation with involved suppliers and hence occasional travel for business is required.

Strategic Sourcing & Procurement engages with our supply chain partners to drive their (operational) performance on metrics on the QLTCS domains (Quality, Logistics, Technology, Cost, and Sustainability). The activities of ‘running the business’ are part of the ‘supplier clusters’. Across the cluster teams and regions, the Supply Chain Transformation team runs the ‘changing the business’ activities.

$162,750-238,700

new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Stone Research Foundation is a 501(c)(3) non-profit research institute founded in 1991 by Kevin R. Stone, MD, and dedicated to developing innovative orthopaedic treatments that help people stay active. The organization focuses on research, development, and education to create regenerative therapies that accelerate healing and address arthritis. Its vision is to transform scientific discovery into treatments that prevent, manage, and ultimately cure joint disease. Team members collaborate with clinicians, scientists, and partners to advance impactful, patient-centered solutions in musculoskeletal health. Learn more at www.stoneresearch.org.

Role Description

The Stone Research Foundation pioneers regenerative orthopaedic treatments to treat, prevent, and cure arthritis. We are seeking a Research Program Manager to drive collaborative research activities, translate scientific innovation into meaningful progress, and connect research, regulatory, and funding efforts—advancing groundbreaking discoveries toward the next generation of orthopaedic care. This position will report to the Sr. Director of Research and Operations. This role is full-time onsite.

Key Responsibilities

Research Operations
· Oversee major study operations activities
· Review and manage study budgeting
· Prepare study protocols and design preclinical and clinical studies
· Track regulatory progress and ensure completion of IND-enabling activities
· Maintain all regulatory documents and records
· Perform statistical analyses as needed to report study data for scientific dissemination and publication
· Assist and work closely with the Sr. Director, Research and Operations to execute activities efficiently at a high level
· May require occasional travel to study sites and conferences with the Sr. Leadership

Project and Program Management
· Serve as an adept project manager for all internal and external partnerships
· Set meetings, deadlines, and overall smooth flow of projects
· Create long-term and short-term plans, including setting and tracking milestones and deliverables
· Serve as the point of contact for all SRF research partnerships
· Analyze and account for possible risks when developing project milestones

Funding and Grant Applications
· Coordinate cross-functional efforts across grant application and submission, including milestone-setting and timelines, setting budgets and activities across internal and external partners
· Take ownership of grant writing and submission

Scientific Communication
· Quickly and efficiently compose and edit presentations and manuscripts for publications
· Prepare abstracts, posters, and slides for conference presentations
· Contribute to presentations compiled for key stakeholders, fundraising, and development purposes
· Effectively and efficiently distill complex scientific concepts into digestible communications for non-scientific team members and external stakeholders

Patient Interface
· Obtain IRB consent and enroll patients in studies on occasion, as needed
· Answer patient questions regarding research on an as-needed basis

Qualifications

· Advanced degree (M.S., MPH, etc.) strongly preferred
· Advanced degree with 5+ years of experience or bachelor’s degree and 7+ years of direct experience desired
· Preference for previous orthopaedic research experience; however, any area of research experience will count toward years of experience
· Skilled in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel
· Comfortable conducting statistical analyses and using software including: GraphPad, ANOVA, t-test, and survival analyses
· Deep experience developing study budgets and tracking budget activities
· Regulatory: Comfort with IND and medical device requirements set by FDA and EMA
· Sound understanding of GCP, GMP, and GLP requirements and ICH standards
· Demonstrated experience in grant writing and management
· Proven manuscript and scientific writing experience
· Previous experience in preclinical and clinical experimental design and protocol design
· Project Management tools: preferred experience using Asana
· IRB submission and patient consent experience

Personal Characteristics

· Strong team player with demonstrated experience in leading and contributing to cross-functional teams
· Proactive and self-starting
· Willingness to wear multiple hats, be resourceful, and always think of ways to improve
· Adaptable and a quick thinker

Compensation and Benefits

· $100K+ salary
· Excellent benefits: We pay 100% of all medical, dental, and vision insurance premiums
· Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave

Ride BART to a satisfying career that lets you both: 1) make a difference to Bay Area residents, and 2) enjoy excellent pay, benefits, and employment stability. Job Summary

Pay Rate
:

Non-Rep Salary Grade E09
