The starting negotiable annual salary for this position will be $160,800.00 (minimum) - $202,206.00 (midpoint) to commensurate with education and experience.

Reports To

Senior Manager of Engineering Programs

Days Off

Saturday and Sunday

Who May Apply

All current BART employees and Future BART employees.

Current Assignment

The San Francisco Bay Area Rapid Transit District (BART) is seeking highly qualified candidates for the Project Manager Accessibility position. The ideal candidates will possess results-oriented engineering and construction experience to manage complex capital improvement projects within its Accessibility Improvement Program. This position will be responsible for accessibility planning, design review, code interpretation and regulatory compliance, and managing the AIP. They will provide District staff with guidance in accessibility and inclusive design principles including communicating and coordinating with internal and external stakeholders to achieve optimal accommodation for all users.

Key responsibilities include defining project scope and budget; managing design teams and resolving stakeholder concerns; supporting procurement activities; and overseeing construction management teams through project closeout to successfully deliver the AIP program.

The position serves as the District’s lead accessibility resource, reviewing and advising on projects, policies, and procedures to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements and industry best practices. The candidates will provide input and assistance in resolving accessibility-related issues across the District’s planning, design, construction, maintenance, and operating entities.

The Most Qualified Candidates For This Position Will Have Highly Developed Competencies In The Following Areas, Which Will Be Reinforced In The Related Work Experience And Will Be Articulated During The Selection Process

Licensed Professional Engineer – Registration as a Professional Civil Engineer in the State of California.
Engineering and Design Expertise – Demonstrated experience managing engineering and/or architectural projects through planning, design, and implementation phases.
Transportation Project Management – Proven experience managing complex projects in an operating transportation, transit, or public infrastructure environment.
Accessibility and Inclusive Design – Extensive knowledge of accessibility regulations and inclusive design best practices.
Communication and Stakeholder Engagement – Excellent written and verbal communication skills and strong public speaking ability.

Selection and Application Process

All applicants must apply online at www.bart.gov/jobs
. Applications must be completed in full and include all requested information, including dates of employment, positions held, hours worked, and a detailed description of duties performed.

Applicants may attach a resume to provide supplemental information; however, the resume does not substitute for completing the application form in its entirety. Only information included in the application at the time of submission will be used to determine whether applicants meet the minimum qualifications for the position. All application materials must be submitted by the closing date and time listed on the job announcement. Applications received after the closing deadline will not be considered.

Applicants who require assistance with the online application process may contact the Talent Acquisition Division
at (510) 464-6112 or employment@bart.gov .

The selection process for this position may include one or more of the following: a skills or performance demonstration, written examination, and/or panel or individual interview.

All applications will be reviewed by the Talent Acquisition Division to determine whether applicants meet the established Minimum Qualifications (MQs). Applicants who meet the MQs may be referred to the hiring department for further evaluation as part of the selection process.

The selected candidate must demonstrate a work history reflecting reliability and dependability and may be required to provide copies of certificates, diplomas, or other documentation required by law, including proof of authorization to work in the United States.

Pre-employment processing will include a background check. This requirement does not apply to current full-time District employees unless the position requires additional evaluations or clearances.

Examples of Duties

Manages BART’s Accessibility Improvement Program’s engineering design and construction projects or programs in assigned areas from conceptual design through completion; project areas may include rail car procurement and rehabilitation, stations construction and rehabilitation, automated fare collection, and transit systems and structures design and construction.
Develops and directs project work standards from design through final program and equipment acceptance.
Develops and directs the implementation of goals, objectives, policies and procedures in assigned project areas.
Plans, organizes, assigns, reviews and evaluates the work of assigned District and contract staff; manages and directs the work of contract consultants.
Directs or participates in the preparation and review of designs, plans, specifications and cost estimates; ensures specifications and contract requirements comply with District standards and policies.
Identifies equipment or systems needs on assigned projects; evaluates functional requirements; reviews vendor and manufacturer design and specifications on project equipment and materials; coordinates equipment procurement and testing activities; oversees equipment installation.
As assigned, oversees contractor and consultant contracts; develops scope of work; prepares request for proposal; reviews proposals and makes recommendation on selection; assists in contract negotiation and preparation; monitors work activities to ensure compliance with contractual obligations.
Manages design and construction management teams.
Performs construction project management duties; prepares cost estimates; prepares and monitors project schedules and budgets; conducts field inspections as required; monitors work in progress; writes, approves, negotiates and executes contract changes; authorizes contract payments upon project completion.
Serves as the project liaison with other divisions, departments and outside agencies; negotiates and resolves project issues.
Provides responsible staff assistance for higher level management staff on projects and related matters.
Attends and participates in professional group meetings; stays abreast of new trends and innovations in the field of engineering design and construction.
Facilitates training workshops for District staff and consultants.
Oversees and directs maintenance of District wide Braille Station Signage – Accessibility Policy Committee, Platform Edge Warning Tile Standards.

Education

Minimum Qualifications

Possession of a bachelor's degree in engineering or related field from an accredited college or university.

Experience

The equivalent of five (5) of professional verifiable experience in transit accessibility, project management or related experience.

Other Requirements

Professional Engineering (PE) license is required.

Substitution

Additional professional experience as outlined above may be substituted for the education on a year-for- year basis. A college degree is preferred.

Knowledge And Skills

Knowledge of:

Principles and practices of engineering disciplines in assigned project area
Principles and practices of engineering design and construction in assigned project area
Principles and practices of project management
Principles and practices of contract administration
Principles and practices used in the preparation of designs, plans, specifications and cost estimates
Principles and practices of strategic planning
Methods and techniques of coordinating and scheduling project work
Methods and techniques of contract negotiation
Principles and practices of procurement
Principles and practices of budget development and administration
Principles of supervision, training and performance evaluation
Current office procedures, methods and equipment including computers
Related Federal, State and local codes, laws and regulations

Skill/Ability in:

Managing, supervising and coordinating assigned projects
Developing and implementing project goals, objectives and procedures
Planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating the work of professional staff and contract consultants
Planning, organizing, scheduling, monitoring and reviewing project work
Managing project design concepts and solutions
Managing and reviewing project budget analysis, calculations and cost estimates
Preparing designs, plans, specifications and cost estimates
Directing or conducting contract negotiations
Conducting field inspections
Developing and administering project budgets
Analyzing problems, identifying alternative solutions, projecting consequences of proposed actions and implementing recommendations in support of goals
Interpreting and explaining established policies and procedures for assigned District projects
Preparing clear and concise reports
Operating office equipment including computers and supporting word processing and spreadsheet applications
Communicating clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing
Establishing and maintaining effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work

new_jobs.title: Project Manager HCI
new_jobs.description:
Company Description

Founded in 1961, WWF works to help people and nature thrive. As a global conservation organization, WWF operates in more than 100 countries, partnering with communities, companies, and governments to protect wildlife, conserve vital habitats, and advance sustainable solutions. Grounded in science and driven by collaboration, WWF works to help nature by conserving biodiversity, supporting resilient communities, and addressing climate change. Nearly 1 million people in the United States and more than 5 million globally are WWF members.

Project Description

The Heart of Conservation Initiative
( HCI
) is a 5-year
global project
designed to address systemic barriers that limit Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ ability to steward their lands, territories, waters, and biodiversity-rich ecosystems. Despite strong evidence that Indigenous Peoples and local communities manage or influence at least 37% of remaining natural lands globally, they receive less than 1% of international climate and biodiversity finance, face complex donor procedures, limited direct access to funding, and insufficient recognition in decision-making arenas.  

Building on the achievements of the GEF-7 Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI), HCI’s objective is to increase Indigenous Peoples’ and local communities’ organizational capacities and ability to access sustainable finance at scale for territorial stewardship to deliver social, economic, cultural, and Global Environmental Benefits. The project is transformative in that it targets structural change in biodiversity finance systems—shifting from centralized, intermediary-driven models toward more inclusive, Indigenous Peoples and local community-led financing and governance mechanisms. 

This will be achieved through four integrated components: (i) organizational and technical self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community funds and organizations and implementation of self-determined Indigenous Peoples- and local community-led sub-projects across Latin America, Africa, and Asia; (ii) collective self-strengthening of Indigenous Peoples and local community-led funds and organizations’ institutional, fiduciary, and technical capacities; (iii) enhancing Indigenous Peoples' and local communities’ representation and influence in global biodiversity and biodiversity finance processes; (iv) advancing knowledge, learning, and evidence on rights-based, inclusive conservation; and (v) monitoring and evaluation.

Job Description

LOCATION: This position will be based in Brazil, Kenya, or Cambodia.

Major Function

The Project Manager will lead the GCU’s support for the HCI partners and ensure successful delivery of all components. They will supervise staff in a Global Coordination Unit (GCU), provide day-to-day management of the project and, with support from the Partner Liaison, coordinate with ten (10)  Component 1 Partners, and partners and specialists in Components 2 through 5.  This is a unique role managing and representing a global, Indigenous-led project that should respond both to Indigenous Peoples and local community partners’ priorities as well as meet GEF requirements. 

The Project Manager will report to the Senior Director, Conservation Areas, and Senior Director, Inclusive Conservation (Project Co-Leads)

Key Responsibilities

 Technical Delivery of Project Components:  
Component 1: Work with Component 1 partners to review and approve their annual work plans and budgets, provide technical inputs to their on-the-ground work, as needed, and support their self-strengthening plans.    
Component 2: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 2 with GCU staff support; Work with Component 1 partners to identify common capacity-strengthening needs and develop and implement a collective strengthening program.  
Component 3: Lead and coordinate delivery of Component 3 with GCU staff support; Design and implement the Youth Policy Leaders program and work with Component 1 and 2 partners to identify policy processes and to enable effective, HCI-supported engagement therein.  
Support GCU staff to ensure successful delivery of Components 4 and 5.
 Project Management: 
Day-to-day management, monitoring, and evaluation of project activities and results as outlined in the CERDoc, Grant Agreement, and Annual Work Plan and Budget to achieve the project objective and targets in the Results Framework. 

Responsibilities will include, but not be limited to:  

Ensure that the GCU holds regular virtual meetings with Component 1 (C1) partners and as required with additional partners involved in the other components,  
Manage the workflow for the Indigenous Global Steering Committee (IGSC), in collaboration with the Project Co-Leads. 
In collaboration with all project sub-grantees and partners, develop the Annual Work Plan and Budget (AWPB) for the global HCI for each project year, for no-objection from the WWF GEF Agency and approval by the IGSC.  
Share C1 Partners’ annual workplans and budgets for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency and for IGSC information.  Provide high-level oversight and monitoring of procurement and expenditure in line with the AWPB in collaboration with the Finance and Operations (FO) Manager.
Review progress of work plan and monitoring plan in collaboration with the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer.  
Responsible for organization of inception workshop and other critical project workshops and meetings. 
Manage the design and maintenance of a project website, and the development and implementation of a communications strategy in collaboration with the Communications and Knowledge Management (CKM) Officer. 
Provide support for project implementation support and learning visits and internal and external reviews/evaluations with relevant GCU staff.
Support the MEL Officer to organize annual reflection workshops to identify lessons learned and propose potential changes for adaptive management to ensure project results and indicator targets are reached. 
Troubleshoot with GCU staff, component partners and Project co-leads to address challenges and create enabling conditions for trusting partnerships and project success.
Maintain a project risk register, including identification of risks to project success and development of mitigation measures in coordination with C1 partners and other project partners.  
Prepare and execute a project exit plan, including hand-off of project equipment and resources, close of grants and agreements, consultations and communications with project partners and interested parties, and ensure sustainability of project results. 
Champion the promise and achievements of the project, elevating its contributions to systems change and Indigenous Peoples and local community-led partners whenever possible. 
Any other tasks that are relevant to the assignment.
Staff management: 
Supervise the GCU staff including MEL Officer (crosscutting, especially components 1, 4 and 5), FO Manager (crosscutting), Environmental and Social Safeguards Officer (crosscutting, especially component 1), Gender Equality and Social Inclusion Officer (crosscutting , especially component 1), CKM Officer (crosscutting, especially components 2 and 4), Logistics and Administrative Assistant (crosscutting), and any other directly recruited staff or consultants.
Prepare TORs to recruit consultants, staff and sub-contracts in consultation with Project Co-Leads and for no-objection from WWF GEF Agency. 
Reporting: 
Collaborate with the MEL Officer to aggregate information from Component 1 Partner sub-projects and formulate semi-annual Project Progress Reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Prepare workshop reports following the inception and other critical project workshops.
Collaborate with the FO Manager to oversee the preparation and disbursement of sub-grants to Component 1 partners and grants and agreements under the other 4 components.  
Collaborate with the FO Manager to aggregate financial information from C1 Partners and oversee the development of quarterly financial reports and ensure timely delivery to the WWF GEF Agency. 
Collaborate with the WWF network and partners to ensure co-finance reporting on a yearly basis. 
Prepare a Project Close Report.  
Quality Assurance: 
Provide quality assurance for project activities, including sub-grants. 
Provide quality assurance through review of reports and other products from partners, technical specialists, consultants, and staff.
Ensure implementation in line with the GEF and WWF standards and policies. 
Week-long, international travel may be expected on approximately a quarterly basis. 
Partnerships: 
Coordinate with co-financed projects and liaise with project partners to ensure co-financing commitments are realized.  
Attract additional partners and co-financing. 
Ensure smooth coordination and communication among all project partners, and with the Component 1 partners (the latter in collaboration with Partner Liaison). 
Manage stakeholder engagement and ensure gender and social inclusion considerations are fully integrated throughout project implementation in collaboration with the Social and Environmental Safeguards (ESS) and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) Officers.  
Represent the project at conferences, meetings, and workshops. 

Qualifications

Key Competencies

Strategic Collaboration and Leadership. Able to lead and influence large and highly dispersed teams and coalitions, dealing with risk mitigation and conflict management.
Intercultural and adaptive management skills 
Results-oriented project management
Collaboration
Cross-cultural communication

Skills And Abilities

10 years of technical working experience, including at least five years of project management experience.  
Bachelor’s Degree; post-graduate degree in a relevant field preferred. 
At least five years’ experience supporting and working in solidarity with Indigenous people and local community organizations, and a demonstrated track record of culturally sensitive and respectful, community-centered collaboration with Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
Demonstrated ability to interact with Indigenous peoples and local community representatives, senior government, NGO, business, and donor staff. 
Experience with the Convention on Biological Diversity and/or other multilateral agreements and processes, focusing on biodiversity, Indigenous peoples’ and local communities’ rights, and finance. 
Experience delivering technical and financial reporting to donor agencies on large projects. 
Experience managing similar, complex, multi-stakeholder and multi-country projects.
Experience leading a team of staff and coordinating sub-grant partners, ideally across multiple time zones and cultures.  
Technical experience and knowledge in the thematic area of the project, such as Indigenous -led territorial stewardship, community-based sustainable development, etc.   
Knowledge of the Open Standards for the Practice of Conservation, or WWF Project and Program Management Standards, preferred. 
Experience with GEF Projects and GEF knowledge an advantage. 
Written and spoken fluency in English required; advanced proficiency in Spanish, French, or Portuguese – highly preferred.   

Additional Information

Location

The position will be based in Brazil, Cambodia or Kenya.

If applying to work in Brazil or Kenya, applicants must be nationals legally authorized to work in Brazil or Kenya. Employment visa sponsorship and relocation are not provided for Brazil or Kenya.

PLEASE NOTE: If applying to work in Cambodia, nationals from South and Southeast Asian countries who are willing to relocate to Cambodia may also apply, and WWF-Cambodia may be able to support visa sponsorship and relocation costs based on available budget.

Please note:
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the job's location.
Position is not eligible for employment visa sponsorship.

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
PROJECT MANAGER

Remote (U.S)

Company Overview

For more than two decades, our client has built mission-critical software for emergency medical services, fire departments, and public safety agencies across the United States, helping responders document patient care in the field, meet state and national reporting requirements, and move critical data between dispatch systems, medical devices, hospitals, and billing platforms. The company serves agencies ranging from small rural departments to some of the largest metropolitan fire and EMS systems in the country, and it has earned a reputation for configurable software, deep domain knowledge, and responsive, knowledgeable customer support. Backed by a large, long-term software investor, the organization pairs the stability of an established business with the autonomy of a lean, remote-friendly team grounded in accountability, adaptability, and humility, and leadership has made AI adoption a company-wide priority. Now in an active growth phase, the company is investing in its commercial organization, expanding its product capabilities, and strengthening the delivery engine that brings new and existing customers onto its platform, and this role sits at the center of that effort.

Position Overview

New business is accelerating and existing agencies are expanding their use of the platform, so our client is establishing a dedicated, full-time Project Manager within its Professional Services organization. Reporting to the Director of Professional Services and Support, this hire will own a high-velocity portfolio of customer implementations, integrations, and data exports, typically 20 or more concurrent projects at a time. This is a rare opportunity for a project manager with roots in EMS, fire, or public safety software to become the central delivery owner at a respected, mission-driven company. First, the role carries true end-to-end ownership and direct visibility, since the Project Manager serves as each customer’s primary point of contact from kickoff through go-live and revenue is recognized only when a project closes. Second, it keeps the hire close to the field, leading training for the administrators and frontline responders who rely on the software every day while working hands-on with the technical setup behind each deployment. Third, it offers a clear path toward senior-level scope in process improvement, product partnership, and the design of new implementation offerings, supported by a well-documented delivery playbook of project templates, work instructions, and training videos that allows a strong hire to ramp quickly. The position is remote within the U.S. with 10% to 20% travel and occasional early morning or evening go-lives across U.S. time zones.

Position Responsibilities

Own a portfolio of 20 or more concurrent implementation, integration, and data export projects from kickoff through go-live, driving each one to customer sign-off on time and within budget so that completed work converts to recognized revenue.
Build project plans from established templates in the team’s project management platform, and improve existing templates or create new ones as the company introduces new implementation and integration offerings.
Track actual hours and tasks against estimates, report variance, and manage scope and risk proactively, escalating to leadership with a clear recommendation before issues turn into delays.
Serve as the primary point of contact for each customer, leading kickoffs, status meetings, and go-lives with agency administrators, clinicians, and leadership, and keeping customers and internal stakeholders aligned through consistent, transparent status reporting.
Design and deliver administrator and end-user training, primarily remote with occasional on-site sessions, so that agency users reach go-live confident and capable on the platform.
Reset customer expectations directly and with tact when scope or timelines shift, protecting long-term relationships while keeping projects moving toward completion.
Configure the product, set up data imports, and execute standard exports such as billing and state reporting files, troubleshooting configuration and data issues hands-on before escalating and building the functional and technical expertise to take on more of this work independently over time.
Coordinate complex integrations, including CAD and third-party vendor connections, by gathering requirements from customers and vendors and giving internal developers what they need to deliver, while explaining technical decisions in plain language to non-technical stakeholders.
Identify customer needs for add-on modules, additional agencies, integrations, and training during implementations and post-go-live check-ins and hand qualified leads to Sales, while supporting presales efforts with scoping, hour estimates, statements of work, and product demonstrations.
Apply AI tools to streamline delivery, documentation, and training content, share lessons learned with Professional Services and Product leadership, and partner with the support team on post-go-live handoffs, tier-2 support within areas of expertise, and occasional backup coverage.

Required

Position Qualifications

A proven track record of delivering customer software implementations on time and within budget, with the ability to cite personal on-time and on-budget performance.
3+ years of project management or software implementation experience, including independent ownership of multiple concurrent customer projects from kickoff through go-live.
Experience with an EMS, fire, public safety, or GovTech software provider, or in closely related healthcare data work such as EMS billing, health data exchange, or emergency department and prehospital EHR implementations.
Hands-on experience building project plans and tracking hours against estimates in a dedicated project management platform, along with working knowledge of CRM tools.
A track record of delivering software training to administrator and end-user audiences, both remotely and in person.
Working knowledge of SaaS applications, system integrations, and data exchange methods such as APIs, web services, and SFTP, with hands-on experience configuring products, setting up data imports, and personally resolving data or integration issues.

Preferred

A field or clinical background as an EMT, paramedic, firefighter, or clinician is strongly preferred, along with familiarity with NEMSIS and state EMS reporting requirements, PMP, CAPM, or Agile training, and healthcare IT or HIPAA-regulated data experience.
A self-sufficient, highly organized working style that keeps many projects moving without close oversight, paired with the credibility to connect with frontline medics and firefighters as easily as agency leadership and an eagerness to adopt AI and new tools.

Ready to make an impact?

Apply now and a member of Talentfoot’s recruitment team will be in touch should your implementation track record, public safety software experience, skills, and qualifications match our client’s requirements.

Talentfoot Overview

Talentfoot Executive Search specializes in future proofing organizations by securing forward-thinking leaders across sales, marketing, eCommerce, product, data, operations, finance, and technology with a track record of accelerating growth, innovation, and profitability. Since 2010, we’ve partnered with more than 2,500 companies and lead the industry with a 98% client success rate. Learn more at Talentfoot.com

new_jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, Global Engineering Services, Startup
new_jobs.description:
Description

Pourquoi Amazon ? Amazon a été désigné comme l'un des meilleurs lieux de travail dans le Corporate Equality Index de la Human Rights Campaign et dans le classement Top Companies de LinkedIn ; a été reconnu dans le Equity, Inclusion, and Empowerment Index de la NAACP ainsi que dans le Disability Equality Index ; et a reçu le 2019 American Foundation for the Blind Helen Keller Achievement Award. Découvrez davantage de nos récompenses et distinctions ici. La culture d'inclusion d'Amazon est renforcée par nos 16 Principes de Leadership, qui rappellent aux membres de l'équipe de rechercher des perspectives diverses, d'apprendre et de faire preuve de curiosité, et de gagner la confiance. Le poste Souhaitez-vous rejoindre une équipe où vous gérerez l'expansion, l'aménagement et le lancement des opérations de Centres de Distribution (FC) à la pointe de la technologie, qui sont à la base du succès d'Amazon et soutiennent nos clients dans un environnement dynamique et en pleine croissance ?

Avec, en prime, la possibilité de voyager et de travailler dans plusieurs pays et cultures ? Le poste peut être basé n'importe où dans l'UE, avec 50 % du temps consacré à des déplacements liés aux projets, que ce soit au niveau national ou vers d'autres pays de la région EMEA.

En tant que Responsable de Programme Senior expérimenté(e), vous êtes chargé(e) de veiller à ce que les FC soient construits dans les délais et dans le respect du budget, en coordonnant le travail de différentes équipes et parties prenantes. Vous soutiendrez l'expansion continue du réseau de distribution européen d'Amazon, serez responsable de la réussite globale des projets en dirigeant et en influençant des équipes de partenaires commerciaux et de parties prenantes techniques au sein d'une organisation matricielle pour l'exécution des projets sur site. De plus, vous piloterez la stratégie commerciale à long terme grâce à la standardisation au sein de notre réseau. Les candidat(e)s retenu(e)s seront naturellement proactifs/proactives, disposeront de bases solides en Gestion de Projet et auront de l'expérience dans la gestion de grands projets avec des calendriers accélérés. Vous êtes capable de diriger et d'encadrer des ingénieurs de projet, des spécialistes techniques et des chefs de projet dans la coordination des risques et des opportunités en termes de délais, de coûts et de qualité. Vous appréciez d'interagir avec, de piloter et de soutenir à la fois des équipes transverses, des experts du domaine et des individus à tous les niveaux, aussi bien à l'intérieur qu'à l'extérieur des lignes hiérarchiques de l'organisation.

Key job responsibilities

Gérer des projets CAPEX au sein d'une organisation pluridisciplinaire et multiculturelle pour nos opérations de distribution clients
Prise en charge de bout en bout des livrables des projets d'entrepôt
Planification intégrée des projets, planification des ressources, analyse du chemin critique et optimisation du calendrier de l'ensemble des activités commerciales, techniques, financières et programmatiques sur plusieurs projets
À l'aise dans différents rôles et capable de communiquer et de travailler efficacement avec des experts en Construction, Ingénierie, Opérations, Finance, Achats, Transport ou Droit des contrats
Coordonner de multiples calendriers interdépendants de flux de matériaux et d'installation des fournisseurs
Travailler aux côtés des fournisseurs et des services achats pour gérer les bons de commande
Maintenir une cadence régulière avec les équipes internes et les fournisseurs pour planifier et suivre les livrables
Suivi et communication continus de l'état d'avancement des projets, remontée ciblée et opportune des risques et problèmes potentiels auprès de plusieurs équipes et des parties prenantes du projet
Travailler de manière indépendante et autonome dans un environnement dynamique et en évolution rapide

A day in the life

Vous planifierez et exécuterez le business case qui permet de livrer des centres de distribution opérationnels. Votre journée pourrait inclure des échanges avec tous les niveaux de l'organisation pour convenir d'une stratégie, vous rendre sur le site et prendre en charge son développement, d'un terrain nu (greenfield) jusqu'à un FC pleinement fonctionnel, planifier et gérer les ressources pour exécuter les activités que vous aurez détaillées dans un calendrier de bout en bout. Vous prendrez des décisions au nom de l'entreprise et verrez leurs résultats se concrétiser grâce à la coordination des parties prenantes, internes comme externes, pour enfin célébrer le lancement réussi de l'installation… le Jour Un pour nous tous !

About The Team

L'équipe EU Startup est composée d'un groupe talentueux de chefs de projet et de programme qui pilotent la coordination de toutes les activités nécessaires à la construction, en toute sécurité, de FC hautement complexes conformes aux standards du réseau sur l'ensemble du marché de l'UE. Notre équipe accorde une grande importance à l'équilibre entre vie professionnelle et vie privée et nous nous consacrons au développement et au soutien de nos nouveaux membres. Cela permet aux Chefs de Projet/Programme de respecter des délais exigeants et des budgets frugaux pour livrer rapidement des projets de construction neuve, d'expansion et de rénovation découlant des besoins en capacité, en stock, en automatisation et en durabilité, afin d'améliorer l'expérience client, de réduire les coûts et d'optimiser le réseau de distribution d'Amazon.

Basic Qualifications

Diplôme de licence (Bachelor) en management, administration des affaires, économie, ingénierie ou marketing
Expérience de travail transverse avec des équipes techniques et non techniques
Expérience en gestion de comptes, gestion de projet/programme ou achats
Expérience dans l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de standards, de politiques et de programmes, ou équivalent
Expérience de la prise en charge de la stratégie de programme, de la livraison de bout en bout et de la communication des résultats à la direction senior
Parler, écrire et lire couramment l'anglais au niveau C1 ou supérieur
Management, coaching et développement de managers, d'équipes et de ressources de projet
Gestion de projets d'infrastructure
Maîtrise des produits Microsoft Office : Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint et MS Project
Expérience de base avec un logiciel de CAO (par ex. AutoCAD, Solid Works ou autre)

Preferred Qualifications

Expérience de la communication avec un large éventail de parties prenantes, y compris des collègues et la direction, ou expérience de la gestion d'équipes
Expérience de la réalisation de tâches complexes rapidement avec peu ou pas d'accompagnement et capacité à réagir avec l'urgence appropriée aux situations nécessitant un traitement rapide, ou expérience de la gestion d'équipes
Expérience dans un environnement logistique/opérationnel
Certification Project Management Professional (PMP) ou équivalente
Expérience dans des tâches ou environnements commerciaux, ou expérience avec les produits et applications Microsoft Office
Parler, écrire et lire couramment le français et l'anglais au niveau C1 ou supérieur
Expérience dans l'e-commerce, le retail ou la publicité,

Amazon est un employeur engagé pour l'égalité des chances. Nous sommes convaincus qu'une main d'oeuvre diversifée est essentielle à notre réussite. Nous prenons nos décisions de recrutement en fonction de votre expérience et de vos compétences. Nous apprécions votre envie de découvrir, d'inventer, de simplifier et de construire. La protection de votre vie privée et la sécurité de vos données constituent depuis longtemps une priorité absolue pour Amazon. Veuillez consulter notre Politique de Confidentialité pour en savoir plus sur la façon dont nous collectons, utilisons et traitons les données personnelles de nos candidats.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

Job Description:

GDIT is seeking a Program Manager - Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) / Counter-Unmanned Aerial Systems (CUAS) to lead the delivery of enterprise-scale capabilities that protect personnel, facilities, and operations.

The Program Manager will integrate strategy, governance, acquisition support, systems engineering, operations, training, sustainment, compliance, and stakeholder engagement into a unified program that supports mission objectives. Success requires experience leading complex UAS and CUAS programs, advancing organizational capabilities, integrating emerging technologies, and driving operational adoption across large federal environments.

HOW A PROGRAM MANAGER - UAS / CUAS WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

Strategic Leadership & Branch Program Governance

Develop and execute multi-year program strategies, capability roadmaps, implementation plans, and performance metrics aligned to mission priorities.
Advise Government leadership on investments, resource requirements, risks, and opportunities to expand and optimize UAS/CUAS capabilities.
Lead an integrated program management structure that aligns technical, operational, acquisition, logistics, security, training, and financial activities.
Establish effective governance, executive reporting, risk management, integrated scheduling, and performance tracking processes.

Program Delivery & Capability Advancement

Direct the full lifecycle delivery of UAS and CUAS initiatives, including development requirements, market research, testing, fielding, operations, sustainment, and continuous improvement.
Advance organizational capability maturity through assessments, gap analysis, workforce planning, process development, and operational integration.
Develop and maintain concepts of operations, standard operating procedures, deployment plans, readiness criteria, lifecycle management processes, and configuration controls.
Manage concurrent efforts across multiple stakeholders and locations while maintaining alignment to cost, schedule, performance, security, and mission objectives.
Lead change management, communications, and knowledge transfer activities that support durable mission outcomes.

Technology Integration, Evaluation & Vendor Management

Support evaluation, selection, integration, and sustainment of UAS/CUAS sensors, command-and-control systems, communications, effectors, data services, and supporting infrastructure.
Apply expertise across leading UAS/CUAS hardware, software, integration, and service providers to inform technology decisions.
Establish requirements traceability, technical evaluation criteria, interoperability objectives, acceptance standards, and modernization roadmaps.
Coordinate demonstrations, pilots, operational assessments, testing activities, technical interchange meetings, and after-action reviews.
Manage subcontractor and OEM relationships, including performance, integration dependencies, licensing, sustainment, and supply-chain considerations.

Operations, Readiness, Training & Sustainment

Develop scalable operational models supporting fixed-site, mobile, expeditionary, and event-driven mission requirements, as authorized by the Government.
Establish readiness reporting, maintenance planning, configuration management, asset accountability, technical documentation, and sustainment processes.
Develop training, qualifications, exercise, and proficiency programs for operators, maintainers, analysts, and program personnel.
Implement operational reporting, lessons learned, incident response, and continuous improvement processes to enhance mission effectiveness.
Plan and oversee long-term sustainment and operational support across geographically dispersed locations.

Security, Safety, Policy & Risk Management

Ensure compliance with applicable federal laws, policies, aviation and spectrum requirements, cybersecurity controls, privacy considerations, records management obligations, export controls, and authorities governing CUAS operations.
Collaborate with legal, policy, security, acquisition, intelligence, aviation, cybersecurity, spectrum, facilities, and operational stakeholders to resolve constraints and support program execution.
Integrate cybersecurity, supply-chain risk management, physical security, operational security, system assurance, and safety practices throughout the program lifecycle.
Lead risk management, contingency planning, audit support, corrective actions, and executive-level risk communication.

Financial, Acquisition & Workforce Management

Manage program financial performance, staffing, resource allocation, subcontractor oversight, forecasting, and execution against established baselines.
Support acquisition activities, including market research, technical requirements development, statements of work, evaluation criteria, cost inputs, source selection support, and post-award oversight.
Recruit, develop, and lead multidisciplinary teams spanning program management, operations, engineering, cybersecurity, logistics, training, integration, and field support.
Foster a culture of accountability, safety, compliance, collaboration, innovation, and mission excellence.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO SUCCEED

Education

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, aviation, computer science, cybersecurity, systems engineering, business, program management, or a related discipline required; master’s degree preferred.

Experience

12+ years of progressively responsible program leadership experience supporting complex federal technology, security, aviation, defense, or mission operations programs.

UAS / CUAS Leadership

5+ years leading UAS, CUAS, airspace security, or closely related programs, including demonstrated experience maturing at least one program, office, branch, or enterprise capability from initial concept through sustained operations.

Federal Agency Experience

Demonstrated success advising and supporting a large federal department or agency as it matured UAS / CUAS capabilities, governance, workforce, policy, technology, and operational processes.

Program Scale

Experience leading multidisciplinary, multi-contractor teams; geographically dispersed operations; complex stakeholder environments; and concurrent technical and operational workstreams.

Technical Experience

Working knowledge of UAS / CUAS architectures, sensors, command-and-control, integration, communications, data, testing, deployment, training, logistics, and lifecycle sustainment. Direct experience with solutions from the named providers or comparable industry platforms is strongly preferred.

Acquisition & Compliance

Experience supporting federal acquisition and vendor management and operating within applicable safety, aviation, spectrum, cybersecurity, privacy, supply-chain, and legal/policy constraints.

Certifications

Project Management Professional (PMP) required or must be obtained within an employer-defined period. Relevant UAS, aviation, systems engineering, cybersecurity, or acquisition credentials are preferred.

Executive Communication

Exceptional ability to communicate complex technical, operational, policy, and risk matters to senior Government executives, operational users, contracting officials, and industry partners.

Security Clearance

Current, in-scope investigation allowing ability to obtain a Top Secret clearance.

Location & Travel

National Capital Region hybrid presence with regular on-site customer engagement. CONUS and OCONUS travel is expected, including travel to operational sites, demonstrations, exercises, and industry locations.

PREFERRED DIFFERENTIATORS

Experience developing enterprise UAS / CUAS strategies and roadmaps across both domestic and international operating environments.
Experience with open architecture, multi-vendor integration, technology insertion, test and evaluation, and transition from pilot to sustained operations.
Experience building Government workforce proficiency and transferring program knowledge, data, processes, and technical baselines to federal personnel.
Experience managing sensitive operational technologies and coordinating among legal, policy, intelligence, law-enforcement, aviation, cybersecurity, acquisition, and customer stakeholders.

Job Summary:

PayPal’s in-house B2B Brand and Creative team is hiring a Brand Program Manager to own the planning, governance, and delivery of brand and creative programs for the B2B marketing organization. You'll turn approved briefs into integrated program plans, manage external agency partners, and work across marketing, product, and events to keep high-visibility work on schedule and on brand. You'll also run the operating cadence behind that work and continuously improve how the team delivers. This is a program management role, not a production role.

Job Description:

Essential Responsibilities:

Identify issues and recommend best practices for content creation and management within the team.
Understand merchant needs, strategic goals, and business objectives
Collaborate with team members to develop compelling narratives and visual assets that engage audiences.
Monitor and evaluate the performance of content initiatives and suggest necessary adjustments.
Stay informed about industry trends to ensure content strategies remain relevant and effective.
Collaborate with subject matter experts and maintain regular communication with internal teams
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery of high-quality content

Minimum Qualifications:

5+ years relevant experience and a Bachelor’s degree OR Any equivalent combination of education and experience.

Additional Responsibilities & Preferred Qualifications:

YOUR DAY TO DAY:

Own delivery of brand and creative programs across marketing, product, social, communications, web, and events, from approved brief through launch.
Build and manage timelines, approval gates, and dependencies, and surface risks early to keep high-visibility programs on track.
Manage external creative agencies day to day, including onboarding on process and brand standards, consolidating stakeholder feedback, guiding approvals, and tracking scope and budget.
Partner with the B2B team to develop program roadmaps and scalable operating standards, including intake, review workflows, and accountability structures.
Plan creative capacity against demand, flag constraints early, and apply lessons from past programs to current work.
Use AI-enabled workflows to streamline briefing, documentation, feedback capture, and collaboration, and scale the tools that improve speed and quality.
Keep the merchant at the center of how programs are prioritized and judged.

WHAT SKILLS WILL HELP YOU BE SUCCESSFUL:

Sound creative judgment, with the ability to apply brand standards in reviews and turn feedback from multiple stakeholders into clear, actionable direction.
The ability to bridge creative teams and marketing stakeholders, speaking fluently about both the work and the business.
Strong prioritization: you keep multiple programs moving in parallel, stay composed under pressure, and work independently.
Rigor in planning, documentation, and risk management.

WHAT YOU BRING:

5+ years of program management experience in an in-house creative or brand team, a creative agency, or a marketing organization.
Direct experience managing external creative agencies, including briefing, scope management, feedback consolidation, and delivery accountability.
Track record delivering multi-workstream, cross-functional programs with multiple stakeholders and approval stages.
Working knowledge of B2B digital channels (paid, content, social, email, web), enough to plan realistic timelines, dependencies, and handoffs.
Proficiency with project and collaboration tools such as Asana, Slack, Teams, and Microsoft 365, and comfort reviewing work in Figma.
Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and work across time zones.
Practical fluency with AI tools and a demonstrated interest in improving how teams work.
B2B marketing experience (preferred).
Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, design, business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Description

Shape the future of secure communications for the world's most critical missions. As a Principal Technical Program Manager for SCS TEMEG, you'll define the strategy and lead customers and cross-functional teams to solve problems of high ambiguity and high impact.

Secure Connections Services (SCS), Tactical Edge Mission Engineering Group (TEMEG) designs, develops, and delivers emerging edge capabilities to enable the use of AWS services.

You own the strategic roadmap and drive cross-organizational alignment on priorities and delivery. You leverage deep technical expertise and executive-level stakeholder management to deliver solutions from concept through customer adoption. You bring proven experience architecting large-scale distributed systems and apply that expertise to commercial and government customers. You are data- and metric-driven, and relentlessly focused on performance in resource-constrained environments.

Solve challenging problems that will revolutionize satellite connectivity in the cloud
Work for a recognized leader in supporting space customers with cloud computing
Have direct impact on hundreds, possibly thousands, of users of the AWS secure connections ecosystem.

If you're driven to lead at the intersection of security innovation and mission-critical impact, this is the role for you.

If Arlington, VA (Arlington HQ2)

This role will sit in our new headquarters in Northern Virginia, where Amazon will invest $2.5 billion dollars, occupy 4 million square feet of energy efficient office space, and create at least 25,000 new full-time jobs. Our employees and the neighboring community will also benefit from the associated investments from the Commonwealth including infrastructure updates, public transportation improvements, and new access to Reagan National Airport.

By working together on behalf of our customers, we are building the future one innovative product, service, and idea at a time. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us.

The candidate selected must obtain and maintain a security clearance at the TS/SCI with polygraph level. Upon start, the selected candidate will be sponsored for a commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities

In This Role You Will

Serve as the primary executive interface with customers, translating mission-critical requirements into product roadmap priorities for engineering teams
Drive cross-organizational alignment across product, engineering, sales, and partner teams to deliver integrated solutions
Work across the product, program, engineering, hardware, software, and infrastructure teams to manage requirements, scope, and delivery of worldwide AWS security features and services
Assess risks, anticipate issues, overcome technical obstacles, and make difficult trade-off decisions while managing cost and schedule to drive adoption goals and meet our customer commitments.

Successful candidates will have a strong technical background, be detail oriented, and have excellent problem-solving abilities. You will represent program status to senior leadership. Your program management expertise and operational excellence will influence teams’ decisions and drive secure and scalable solutions. You should be passionate about delivering great customer experiences and changing the way customers leverage AWS services.

Builders at Amazon work on real world problems on a global scale, own their systems end-to-end, and influence the direction of our technology that impacts hundreds of millions customers around the world. Join a team of super smart, customer obsessed builders that think big and have fun.

A day in the life

In this role, you will own the planning and execution of a new service managing cross-team and cross-org development and delivery, participating in architecture decisions, design reviews, and represent our service to Senior and Executive leadership. You will work with software developers and networking engineers along with product managers and other oranizations to deliver new services and new features create the best in class solutions for our customers worldwide!

Candidates must be comfortable with ambiguity and eager to embrace ownership and accountability.

About The Team

About AWS

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Why AWS?

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help our team members develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.

AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS)

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of technical product or program management experience
7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
3+ years of software development experience
5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred Qualifications

5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

new_jobs.title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Inference
new_jobs.description:
CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at www.coreweave.com.

About The Team

The AI/ML TPM team owns delivery and execution across CoreWeave’s AI/ML Platform Services organization. The team partners closely with Product, Engineering, Research, Infrastructure, and Go-to-Market teams to deliver scalable, reliable, and high-performance platforms that support the full AI lifecycle. AI/ML TPMs drive alignment and execution across highly technical, cross-functional teams to ensure the successful delivery of customer-facing infrastructure and platform capabilities used by researchers, engineers, and enterprise customers.

About The Role

CoreWeave’s AI/ML Platform Services organization builds the distributed systems that power large-scale inference workloads across our GPU-accelerated cloud. As a Technical Program Manager focused on inference, you will lead complex, cross-functional programs spanning inference platform delivery, customer onboarding, launch readiness, and runtime optimization.

The Inference team is responsible for building and operating highly scalable, reliable production inference services for both serverless and dedicated inference use cases. The work spans platform reliability, operational excellence, customer onboarding, release validation, runtime performance, and the launch of new inference capabilities that help customers run models at scale with strong price-performance and low operational friction.

In this role, you will partner with engineering, product, infrastructure, and go-to-market teams to drive programs that improve how inference services are launched, onboarded, operated, and optimized. This includes managing the execution of customer-facing onboarding programs, launch readiness for dedicated inference capabilities, and the platform improvements needed to support scale, reliability, and predictable delivery.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in complex, cross-functional environments, has deep technical fluency in distributed systems, inference infrastructure, and AI platform operations, and excels at creating structure, visibility, and execution rhythm across multiple teams.

What You’ll Do

Drive end-to-end program management for inference platform initiatives spanning reliability, customer onboarding, launch readiness, and runtime optimization.
Lead cross-functional programs for customer onboarding across dedicated and serverless inference offerings, ensuring clear ownership, launch criteria, and readiness for strategic customer use cases.
Drive launch readiness for new inference capabilities by aligning teams around real customer outcomes, supportability, and end-to-end validation.
Partner with engineering and product to define and deliver roadmap outcomes for latency, throughput, uptime, operational quality, and price-performance.
Coordinate multi-team execution across platform, infrastructure, and customer-facing teams to deliver reliable and scalable inference services.
Build and operationalize success metrics, dashboards, launch gates, and review cadences to measure service reliability, onboarding readiness, efficiency, and quality across the inference stack.
Establish repeatable processes for release validation, performance regression tracking, launch management, and postmortem follow-through.
Help unify operational processes, support mechanisms, and execution visibility across inference deployment models and customer onboarding paths.
Create strong communication channels between Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Go-to-Market teams to align priorities and deliver predictable, high-impact outcomes.

Who You Are

Bachelor’s degree in a technical field or equivalent practical experience.
8+ years of technical program management experience in distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, or AI/ML platform engineering.
Proven experience driving large-scale infrastructure or platform programs from concept to production in complex, cross-functional environments.
Strong technical fluency in distributed inference systems, GPU compute, cloud-native architectures, and performance optimization.
Demonstrated success driving measurable improvements in reliability, performance, operational readiness, or customer delivery.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to align engineering, product, infrastructure, and customer-facing stakeholders around shared goals.
Experience with inference-serving systems, model onboarding workflows, rollout strategies, and observability tooling.
Familiarity with launch readiness, supportability, incident follow-through, and release validation for production infrastructure or platform services.
Understanding of customer onboarding for technical products, especially where platform capabilities, infrastructure readiness, and support processes must align for launch.
Experience operating in high-growth environments where roadmap execution, reliability expectations, and customer commitments must be managed in parallel.

Wondering if you’re a good fit?

We believe in investing in our people and value candidates who bring diverse experiences to our teams—even if you aren’t a 100% skill or experience match. Here are a few qualities we’ve found compatible with our team. If some of this describes you, we’d love to talk.

You love driving execution for complex, customer-facing AI infrastructure and platform programs.
You’re curious about how large-scale inference systems evolve across runtime performance, operational excellence, and customer onboarding.
You’re effective at creating clarity and momentum across ambiguous, fast-moving multi-team initiatives.
You enjoy turning technically complex platform work into predictable execution and successful launches.

Why CoreWeave?

About

At CoreWeave, we work hard, have fun, and move fast! We’re in an exciting stage of hyper-growth that you will not want to miss out on. We’re not afraid of a little chaos, and we’re constantly learning. Our team cares deeply about how we build our product and how we work together, which is represented through our core values:

Be Curious at Your Core
Act Like an Owner
Empower Employees
Deliver Best-in-Class Client Experiences
Achieve More Together

We support and encourage an entrepreneurial outlook and independent thinking. We foster an environment that encourages collaboration and provides the opportunity to develop innovative solutions to complex problems. As we get set for takeoff, the growth opportunities within the organization are constantly expanding. You will be surrounded by some of the best talent in the industry, who will want to learn from you, too. Come join us!

The base salary range for this role is $177,000 to $237,000. The starting salary will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. We strive for both market alignment and internal equity when determining compensation. In addition to base salary, our total rewards package includes a discretionary bonus, equity awards, and a comprehensive benefits program (all based on eligibility).

What We Offer

The range we’ve posted represents the typical compensation range for this role. To determine actual compensation, we review the market rate for each candidate which can include a variety of factors. These include qualifications, experience, interview performance, and location.

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer a variety of benefits to support your needs. The benefits below reflect our US-based offerings for full-time employees; for roles in other locations, benefits vary and are shared during the hiring process. These include:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance - 100% paid for by CoreWeave

Health Savings Account
Tuition Reimbursement
Ability to Participate in Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)
Mental Wellness Benefits through Spring Health
Family-Forming support provided by Carrot

Flexible, full-service childcare support with Kinside
401(k) with a generous employer match
Flexible PTO
Catered lunch each day in our office and data center locations
A casual work environment
A work culture focused on innovative disruption

Description

Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

The Leo team is looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager with stronge experience in wir3eless communications/networking and embedded software, project management, and program management. The role will interface with cross-functional engineering and program/product management teams with primary focus on delivering top quality Satellite and ground Payload and Data Plane software. Join us and make a difference to people around the world.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities

In This Role You Will

Collaborate with engineering leaders to create project plans for Satellite Payload software development across the entire software stack including data, management plane
Work with product/program management to ensure that development meets schedule, cost, and quality requirements.
Drive engineering project execution, make technical trade-offs, track and report on status, and resolve blocking issues.
Collaborate with architecture, hardware, software, firmware teams on ensuring cross-functional deliverables are identified and tracked.
Aggregate and convert technical specifications for Leo's Satellite Payload and Data Plane software systems
Establish mechanisms to manage scrums, tasks, budgets, dashboards, schedule and overall delivery for the Satellite Payload and Data Plane software
Map HW / SW co-dependencies and track accuracy of plans and technical developments for all major milestones
Work closely across the org on new HW bring up.

A day in the life

In this role, you will build and scale Leo's Satellite Payload and Data Plane software development programs. You are accountable for creating and working the complex multi-subsystem program plan for the development, test and delivery of Leo's Satellite Payload system and Data Plane, and their integration with rest of Leo system for delivering an end-to-end network solution with an exceptional quality of experience for our customers.

The Team is responsible for Architecture, design and delivering and end to end Networking systems for both constellation and ground, as well as the services that utilize the network to delivery last mile and back-haul internet services.

8+ years of hands-on work managing complex technology projects experience

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Veeco

You probably don’t realize it, but what we do at Veeco touches the lives of every person, every day. It’s a bold statement, but it’s true. From the smartphones in our pockets that access the world’s collective knowledge, to the cloud-based services where all that information lives, to high-speed wireless communication and computing power needed to drive artificial intelligence, augmented and virtual reality, gaming and so much more, our technology is all around us.

We design, develop, manufacture, and service highly complex, cutting-edge machines used by our customers to create the essential devices that drive the digital age, connect the world, and improve the human experience. Along with the world’s leading technology companies, many of which are household names, we help solve their most difficult material science challenges, enabling technologies for a more connected, sustainable, and convenient world.

We’re looking for material difference-makers to join our growing team. Interested? Learn more at www.veeco.com/careers .

Overview

Veeco's complex semiconductor equipment programs require disciplined coordination across engineering, supply chain, operations, and customer-facing teams to move new technology from concept to qualified product. As Program Manager, you will lead multidisciplinary programs through design, engineering release, procurement, system integration, testing, qualification, and lifecycle milestones. Your decisions will directly influence schedule performance, product cost, technical readiness, quality, and customer commitments for advanced vacuum process equipment. You will create the operating rhythm, visibility, and cross-functional alignment that enable teams to resolve risk early and deliver reliable products to market.

Responsibilities

Own multiple complex engineering and product-development programs from concept through product release, aligning technical scope, schedule, cost, quality, and customer objectives.
Build and maintain integrated program plans that identify milestones, dependencies, critical-path activities, decision points, and recovery actions.
Drive cross-functional decisions across mechanical, electrical, systems, software, process engineering, operations, supply chain, technical support, and field service teams.
Anticipate program risks and lead clear mitigation or recovery plans that protect engineering releases, long-lead procurement, system builds, integration, testing, and qualification milestones.
Establish concise program reviews and dashboards that give engineering and executive leaders timely visibility into schedule performance, milestone variance, cost, technical readiness, and unresolved decisions.
Control product configuration and lifecycle execution by coordinating engineering change orders, bills of material, documentation releases, continuous improvement activities, and customer-specific engineering requirements.
Manage program budgets, product-cost targets, resource needs, and costed bills of material in partnership with functional leaders and supply chain teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering, engineering management, or a related technical discipline.
5+ years of experience in engineering, project management, or technical program management for complex equipment or hardware products.
Experience leading multidisciplinary programs that include mechanical, electrical, software, systems, manufacturing, and supply chain workstreams.
Experience managing product development through engineering release, procurement, system integration, testing, and qualification.
Experience independently managing multiple programs with competing schedules, resources, and priorities.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Skilled at translating complex technical work into integrated schedules, critical-path analysis, measurable milestones, and practical recovery plans.
Working knowledge of semiconductor capital equipment, vacuum processing systems, or other complex manufacturing equipment.
Proficiency with engineering change control, bills of material, product configuration, and product lifecycle processes.
Ability to evaluate technical and business trade-offs, clarify decision ownership, and guide cross-functional teams toward timely resolution.
Skilled at presenting concise program status, risks, priorities, and decisions to engineers, suppliers, customers, and senior leaders.
Experience with enterprise resource planning and product lifecycle management systems, such as SAP, and scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project or Smartsheet.
Project Management Professional certification or experience with customer-specific and engineer-to-order programs is preferred.

Salary And Benefits

The expected salary range for this position is $106,548.00 — $142,064.00, plus a bonus opportunity. We will consider your location, experience, and other job-related factors when determining your pay.

Other Benefits Include

Medical, Dental, and Vision
401(k) with Company Match
Holiday, Vacation, and Sick Time
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
Commuter Benefits
Life and Accident Insurance
Disability Insurance
Tuition Reimbursement
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Identity Theft Remediation
Emergency Travel Assistance

new_jobs.title: Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies’ core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

This role supports our Defense Systems business, bringing together Hypersonics, Strategic Missile Defense, Tactical Missiles, and Integrated Defense Systems. Modern defense missions demand more than piecemeal parts or patchwork products; they require hardware that seamlessly integrates disparate technologies into a unified system. Backed by decades of flight-proven performance, our teams deliver tailored mission-ready solutions across air, land, and sea, including: launch and deployment systems, propulsion, payload protection, integration and deployment.

In this role, you will lead defense programs through planning, development, qualification, production, and delivery. You will develop integrated program plans, manage performance against cost and schedule, coordinate cross-functional execution, and serve as a primary interface with customers and internal stakeholders. Your work ensures the successful delivery of mission-critical missile, propulsion, launch, payload, and defense-system hardware.

Schedule

This role follows a 9/80 schedule, with 9-hour shifts Monday through Thursday, an 8-hour shift every other Friday, and the alternating Friday off.

Responsibilities

Leads assigned programs through planning, development, qualification, production, delivery, and contract completion.
Owns performance against cost, schedule, technical, quality, contractual, and customer objectives.
Develops and maintains integrated program plans, schedules, budgets, milestones, resource requirements, and performance metrics.
Coordinates cross-functional execution across engineering, operations, quality, supply chain, contracts, finance, and test.
Serves as a primary program interface for customers, prime contractors, government stakeholders, suppliers, and internal leadership.
Identifies technical, programmatic, supply-chain, cost, and schedule risks and drives mitigation and recovery plans.
Leads recurring program reviews and communicates financial performance, risks, decisions, dependencies, and corrective actions.
Supports design reviews, test‑readiness reviews, qualification activities, production‑readiness reviews, and customer acceptance events.
Manages contractual deliverables, statements of work, program changes, customer requests, and scope changes.
Supports proposals, estimates, contract negotiations, follow‑on opportunities, and program‑growth activities.
Performs other related duties as needed.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business program management, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience.
At least 5 years of experience supporting or managing aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, or similarly complex technical programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a related technical field or a Master of Business Administration (MBA).
Experience managing Department of Defense, U.S. government, allied‑defense, or prime‑contractor programs.
Experience with missile systems, propulsion, launch systems, payload integration, separation systems, energetic devices, or related flight hardware.
Experience managing programs from development through qualification and production.
Knowledge of government contracting and fixed‑price, cost‑reimbursable, or incentive‑based contract structures.
Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM), cost‑account management, or similar financial‑performance methods.
Experience supporting proposals, estimates, negotiations, contract modifications, or follow‑on program capture.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent formal program‑management training.
Experience with program scheduling, enterprise resource planning (ERP), or product‑lifecycle management (PLM) systems.
Experience leading engineering teams to develop mechanical and pyrotechnic components and systems.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

Make the world’s most advanced Undersea Systems even smarter

ROLE AND POSITION OBJECTIVES:

You will partner with the program manager, chief engineer, and functional leads to align technical scope, schedule, resources, risks, and deliverables across optical, electrical, mechanical, software, systems, and test disciplines.
